POSSIBLE HYBRID WORKPLACE OPPORTUNITY
New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) is the State’s affordable housing agency, with a mission to build, preserve, and protect affordable housing and increase homeownership throughout New York State.
This position is with HCR's Housing Trust Fund Corporation (HTFC). This is not a civil service position and does not require a civil service exam. Candidates must meet the minimum qualifications outlined below to be considered. 
NYS Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) is committed to fostering a culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility. Our work would not be possible without the diverse backgrounds, experiences, ideas, and abilities of our employees. HCR is committed to developing a workforce that represents the diverse population of New York State. HCR embraces a diverse and inclusive work environment by encouraging all individuals, including those with disabilities, to apply to open positions at the agency.
Resilient Homes and Communities (RHC) now serves as the lead principal office responsible for the administration of New York State’s multiple CDBG-DR awards. RHC operates within the New York State Housing Trust Fund Corporation (HTFC) and the Homeownership and Community Development (HOCD) unit, which consists of the State of New York Mortgage Agency, the Affordable Housing Corporation, the Office of Community Renewal, the Office of Special Initiatives and RHC.
Position Summary
The Data Analyst will play a key supporting role analyzing, visualizing and reporting data for the Office of Resilient Homes and Communities. This position combines data science, spatial data analysis (GIS) with business and policy research to support reporting, decision-making, and program quality across the agency. Reporting to the Director of Research and Data, the Data Analyst will assist in maintaining spatial and quantitative databases, updating the federal Disaster Recovery Grants Reporting (DRGR) system, and producing maps, dashboards, and reports. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional to gain hands-on experience in disaster recovery policy, data integrity, and public sector data analysis.
Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

 Data & Reporting Support: Assist in the development, update, and maintenance of performance management reports, dashboards, and ad hoc data analyses to support program operations.
 GIS & Spatial Analysis: Support program teams by maintaining Esri ArcGIS software/ArcGIS Online platforms, performing basic spatial analyses, and creating maps and graphs for internal and external stakeholders.
 System Maintenance: Help input, track, and verify service areas and program data within New York State’s internal systems and the federal Disaster Recovery Grant Reporting (DRGR) system to ensure accuracy across program records.
 Data Quality & Documentation: Assist in documenting data methodologies, maintaining Standards of Procedure (SOPs) for federal reporting, and performing routine data cleaning and quality control.
 Research Assistance: Provide analytical and research support for ongoing projects evaluating the impact of RHC programs on New York State residents.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with internal program teams and external partners to share, transfer, and package data for reporting and research needs.

Qualifications:

 Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Geography, Urban Planning, Public Policy, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field*
 Knowledge of public policy in areas such as disaster recovery, infrastructure, housing, economic development, and/or resiliency is preferred.
 Experience distilling quantitative and qualitative policy analysis into written descriptions such as briefs, memos, etc.
 2 years professional experience in an analytic role*
 Demonstrated experience using Esri ArcGIS 10.x, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Server, Model Builder, R and basic python programming. 
 Excellent oral, written, and quantitative skills.
 Exceptional problem-solving abilities. 
 Exceptional ability to use data to make decisions. 
 Expertise in the use of Microsoft Office products, specifically Excel and Access.
 Ability to work in a flexible, fast paced, mission driven environment.

*Substitutions: four years of specialized experience or associate’s degree and two years of specialized experience may substitute for bachelor’s degree; J.D. or master’s degree may substitute for one year of specialized experience; Ph.D. may substitute for two years of specialized experience.
This job description is not intended to be all inclusive and the employee will be expected to perform other reasonably related duties as assigned.
APPLICANTS MUST INCLUDE A RESUME
WHAT WE OFFER AT NYS HCR: 

 Extensive benefits package including participation in New York State’s Health Insurance Program and New York State & Local Employees’ Retirement System.
 Promotional opportunities for dedicated professionals.
 Work-life balance benefits including a 37.5-hour work week, opportunity for compressed scheduling, and paid time off benefits (vacation, sick, personal days, and federal holidays).
 12 weeks of Paid Parental Leave.
 Paid Family Leave.
 As a New York State employee, you may qualify to participate in the Federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). The PSLF Program forgives the remaining balance on your Direct Loans after you have made 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan and while working full-time for an eligible employer. 

ABOUT NEW YORK STATE HOMES AND COMMUNITY RENEWAL:
Under the leadership of Governor Kathy Hochul and Commissioner RuthAnne Visnauskas, HCR is a vibrant, innovative agency that integrates and leverages New York State’s housing resources. We have offices in New York City, Albany, Buffalo, and Syracuse, and employ a diverse workforce of professionals who are hard-working and committed to serving low- and moderate-income families. Our mission is far-reaching, encompassing single and multifamily housing finance, home improvement, rent regulation, housing subsidies, and community development. We partner regularly with a variety of public and private stakeholders.
Achieving this mission requires a wide range of skills and backgrounds in public policy, administration, real estate, construction, finance, law, and many other areas of expertise. We seek to provide a workplace environment that is productive, flexible, accountable, ethical, and caring. Our employees are empowered to make a difference where they live and work. We offer competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package, including paid leave, health, dental, vision, retirement, and family-friendly policies. 
New York State is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE)

We support Morgan Stanley to achieve its business goals by partnering with business units across the Firm to realize efficient risk-adjusted returns, acting as a strategic advisor to the Board and protecting the Firm from exposure to losses as a result of credit, market, liquidity, operational, model and other risks.

Associate - AI Governance & Reporting

Position Summary

The Associate will support the delivery of AI-enabled solutions across Model Risk Management (MRM) Governance and Reporting. This role combines Scrum Master responsibilities with hands-on support for identifying, coordinating, and implementing AI-driven process improvements. The individual will work closely with business stakeholders, technology teams, reporting teams, and AI initiatives to accelerate automation, improve operational efficiency, and enhance reporting capabilities across MRM.

This role will play a key part in driving agile delivery practices, managing solution backlogs, coordinating stakeholder engagement, and helping transform governance and reporting processes through innovative AI technologies. The responsibilities closely align with current MRM efforts to expand AI adoption across governance, reporting, inventory management, and workflow automation.

Key Responsibilities

Identify and deliver AI and automation opportunities across MRM governance, reporting, inventory management, and policy assurance.

Support policy assurance activities, including monitoring compliance, findings, remediation actions, exceptions, and governance commitments.

Support model, Tool, and EUC inventory governance, including attestations, verifications, data-quality reviews, discrepancy resolution, control monitoring, and reporting.

Prepare dashboards, metrics, executive summaries, presentations, and other materials for senior management and governance forums.

Support MRM training, communications, FAQs, procedures, templates, and stakeholder guidance.

Document requirements and coordinate cross-functional testing, implementation, adoption, and stakeholder communication.

Facilitate Agile ceremonies, maintain backlogs and delivery roadmaps, and track milestones, dependencies, risks, impediments, and delivery metrics.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business, technology, data analytics, finance, risk management, or a related field.

1-4 years of experience in Agile delivery, project coordination, business analysis, reporting, governance, risk management, or technology.

Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and stakeholder-management skills.

Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills.

Familiarity with Agile and Scrum practices.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI, GenAI, automation, Power BI, Jira or similar tools.

Experience in financial services, governance, risk management, reporting, or inventory oversight.

Scrum Master or project-coordination experience.

What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser.

Expected base pay rates for the role will be between $100,000 and $140,000 year at the commencement of employment. However, base pay if hired will be determined on an individualized basis and is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, incentive compensation, discretionary bonuses, other short and long-term incentive packages, and other Morgan Stanley sponsored benefit programs.

Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents.

At Moody's, we unite the brightest minds to turn today’s risks into tomorrow’s opportunities. We do this by striving to create an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome to be who they are—with the freedom to exchange ideas, think innovatively, and listen to each other and customers in meaningful ways. Moody’s is transforming how the world sees risk. As a global leader in ratings and integrated risk assessment, we’re advancing AI to move from insight to action—enabling intelligence that not only understands complexity but responds to it. We decode risk to unlock opportunity, helping our clients navigate uncertainty with clarity, speed, and confidence.

If you are excited about this opportunity but do not meet every single requirement, please apply! You still may be a great fit for this role or other open roles. We are seeking candidates who model our values: invest in every relationship, lead with curiosity, champion diverse perspectives, turn inputs into actions, and uphold trust through integrity.

Skills And Competencies

Strong theoretical grounding in econometrics, statistics, machine learning, and other quantitative modeling approaches, with demonstrated ability to determine when traditional, machine-learning, or hybrid methods are most appropriate, based on business context, data availability, and interpretability needs [Required]Experience working with large, real-world datasets: cleaning, merging, exploring, and diagnosing data problems [Required]Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with demonstrated ability to distill complex modeling concepts into clear, audience-appropriate messages for senior leaders, cross-functional partners, and non-technical stakeholders [Required]Strong programming skills in Python or R, plus working knowledge of SQL [Required]Fluency with AI productivity tools including coding agents [Required]Adaptable and curious: comfortable moving between projects and subject areas and learning new domains quickly [Required]Demonstrated proficiency in artificial intelligence concepts, with hands-on experience using AI tools to streamline workflows and enhance operational efficiency. Proven ability to implement AI-powered solutions to solve business challenges. Demonstrates a growing awareness of AI risk management and a commitment to responsible and ethical AI use.Experience in credit risk modeling (e.g., default prediction, early warning, or scoring models) or other financial modeling [Preferred]Knowledge of accounting and financial statement analysis [Preferred]Experience with large-scale data tools and formats such as Spark, Athena, or Parquet, and general database concepts [Preferred]Experience with Git/GitHub in a collaborative development setting [Preferred]Exposure to cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure [Preferred]Familiarity with model documentation and model risk governance standards (e.g., SR 11-7, SR 26-2, etc.) [Preferred]

Education

Master's degree in Financial Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Economics, Econometrics, Mathematics, Physics, Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field with 2 years of industry experience in quantitative modeling [Required]Ph.D. in Financial Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Economics, Econometrics, Mathematics, Physics, Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field [Preferred]CPA [Preferred]

Responsibilities

Drive quantitative modeling innovation at Moody's Credit Center of Excellence to enhance credit analytics and predictive modeling capabilities globally.

Partner across Moody's business lines to enhance modeling and analytical frameworks, incorporating state-of-the-art techniquesDesign and deliver innovative analytical solutions, leveraging quantitative methods to address complex financial, economic, and operational problemsBuild modeling datasets from large, varied sources of financial, market, and firm-level data; assess data quality, handle missing or inconsistent data, and construct sound estimation samplesContribute to the ongoing development of established models, including re-estimation, recalibration, performance analysis, and methodology enhancementsEvaluate when traditional, machine-learning, or hybrid approaches best fit a problem, weighing predictive performance against interpretability, stability, and data limitationsWrite clear model documentation and methodology materials that support internal model governance and client transparencyCommunicate technical subject matter clearly and concisely, ensuring that insights, limitations, and implications are well understood by diverse audiencesContribute to projects across the Credit Center of Excellence as priorities evolve, quickly learning existing models, codebases, and subject areas

About The Team

The Credit Center of Excellence (COE) at Moody's is dedicated to developing, enhancing and maintaining our industry-leading credit analytics and predictive modelling capabilities. Our analytics and models are used by institutions worldwide to make credit, risk management, pricing, and investment decisions. We are a global team (spread across all US time zones, GMT, GMT+1) and we work closely with various teams including product management, commercial strategy, and go-to-market leaders to ensure the delivery of high-quality credit risk assessments and solutions. This collaborative approach allows the COE to integrate seamlessly into Moody's structure to support and grow our customers' business operations and enhance their ability to navigate risk.

New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) is the State’s affordable housing agency, with a mission to build, preserve, and protect affordable housing and increase homeownership throughout New York State.
This position is with HCR's Housing Trust Fund Corporation (HTFC). This is not a civil service position and does not require a civil service exam. Candidates must meet the minimum qualifications outlined below to be considered. 
NYS Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) is committed to fostering a culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility. Our work would not be possible without the diverse backgrounds, experiences, ideas, and abilities of our employees. HCR is committed to developing a workforce that represents the diverse population of New York State. Resilient Homes and Communities (RHC) now serves as the lead principal office responsible for the administration of New York State’s multiple CDBG-DR awards. RHC operates within the New York State Housing Trust Fund Corporation (HTFC) and the Homeownership and Community Development (HOCD) unit, which consists of the State of New York Mortgage Agency, the Affordable Housing Corporation, the Office of Community Renewal, the Office of Special Initiatives and RHC.
Position Summary
The Data Analyst will play a key supporting role analyzing, visualizing and reporting data for the Office of Resilient Homes and Communities. This position combines data science, spatial data analysis (GIS) with business and policy research to support reporting, decision-making, and program quality across the agency. Reporting to the Director of Research and Data, the Data Analyst will assist in maintaining spatial and quantitative databases, updating the federal Disaster Recovery Grants Reporting (DRGR) system, and producing maps, dashboards, and reports. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional to gain hands-on experience in disaster recovery policy, data integrity, and public sector data analysis.
Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

 Data & Reporting Support: Assist in the development, update, and maintenance of performance management reports, dashboards, and ad hoc data analyses to support program operations.
 GIS & Spatial Analysis: Support program teams by maintaining Esri ArcGIS software/ArcGIS Online platforms, performing basic spatial analyses, and creating maps and graphs for internal and external stakeholders.
 System Maintenance: Help input, track, and verify service areas and program data within New York State’s internal systems and the federal Disaster Recovery Grant Reporting (DRGR) system to ensure accuracy across program records.
 Data Quality & Documentation: Assist in documenting data methodologies, maintaining Standards of Procedure (SOPs) for federal reporting, and performing routine data cleaning and quality control.
 Research Assistance: Provide analytical and research support for ongoing projects evaluating the impact of RHC programs on New York State residents.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with internal program teams and external partners to share, transfer, and package data for reporting and research needs.

Qualifications:

 Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Geography, Urban Planning, Public Policy, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field*
 Knowledge of public policy in areas such as disaster recovery, infrastructure, housing, economic development, and/or resiliency is preferred.
 Experience distilling quantitative and qualitative policy analysis into written descriptions such as briefs, memos, etc.
 2 years professional experience in an analytic role*
 Demonstrated experience using Esri ArcGIS 10.x, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Server, Model Builder, R and basic python programming. 
 Excellent oral, written, and quantitative skills.
 Exceptional problem-solving abilities. 
 Exceptional ability to use data to make decisions. 
 Expertise in the use of Microsoft Office products, specifically Excel and Access.
 Ability to work in a flexible, fast paced, mission driven environment.

*Substitutions: four years of specialized experience or associate’s degree and two years of specialized experience may substitute for bachelor’s degree; J.D. or master’s degree may substitute for one year of specialized experience; Ph.D. may substitute for two years of specialized experience.
This job description is not intended to be all inclusive and the employee will be expected to perform other reasonably related duties as assigned.
APPLICANTS MUST INCLUDE A RESUME
WHAT WE OFFER AT NYS HCR: 

 Extensive benefits package including participation in New York State’s Health Insurance Program and New York State & Local Employees’ Retirement System.
 Promotional opportunities for dedicated professionals.
 Work-life balance benefits including a 37.5-hour work week, opportunity for compressed scheduling, and paid time off benefits (vacation, sick, personal days, and federal holidays).
 12 weeks of Paid Parental Leave.
 Paid Family Leave.
 As a New York State employee, you may qualify to participate in the Federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). The PSLF Program forgives the remaining balance on your Direct Loans after you have made 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan and while working full-time for an eligible employer. 

ABOUT NEW YORK STATE HOMES AND COMMUNITY RENEWAL:
Under the leadership of Governor Kathy Hochul and Commissioner RuthAnne Visnauskas, HCR is a vibrant, innovative agency that integrates and leverages New York State’s housing resources. We have offices in New York City, Albany, Buffalo, and Syracuse, and employ a diverse workforce of professionals who are hard-working and committed to serving low- and moderate-income families. Our mission is far-reaching, encompassing single and multifamily housing finance, home improvement, rent regulation, housing subsidies, and community development. We partner regularly with a variety of public and private stakeholders.
Achieving this mission requires a wide range of skills and backgrounds in public policy, administration, real estate, construction, finance, law, and many other areas of expertise. We seek to provide a workplace environment that is productive, flexible, accountable, ethical, and caring. Our employees are empowered to make a difference where they live and work. We offer competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package, including paid leave, health, dental, vision, retirement, and family-friendly policies.

VERSANT (Nasdaq: VSNT) is an industry-changing media and entertainment business and home to trusted brands that shape culture, inform audiences, and build lasting connections. Versant, an industry-leading news, sports and entertainment media business that provides content through a portfolio of iconic television networks (MS NOW, CNBC, USA Network, Golf Channel, E!, SYFY and Oxygen) and complementary digital assets (Fandango, Rotten Tomatoes, GolfNow and SportsEngine), is seeking a Consumer Insights Senior Analyst who is energized by the idea of contributing to the growth of a new company within a fast-paced media landscape.

At Versant, data and consumer insights power how we connect with audiences across entertainment, news, sports, and digital experiences. As a Senior Analyst, Consumer Insights & Analytics, you'll help answer some of our most important business questions by combining consumer research with advanced analytics to uncover meaningful insights that influence strategic decision-making across the organization.

Working within the Consumer Insights team and partnering closely with the broader Data Insights & Strategic Analytics organization, you'll leverage quantitative research, audience data, behavioral analytics, and business intelligence tools to understand consumer behavior, measure brand performance, identify emerging trends, and deliver actionable recommendations.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, thrives in a data-driven environment, and can bridge technical analysis with compelling business storytelling.

Sales is where our brands meet the real world.

The key purpose of the role is to produce actionable insights and reporting in support of the Strategic Insights team and its key stakeholders, leveraging both external and internal data sources.

Produce monthly Nielsen and NABCA trend updates for the broad organization, covering category and brand performance in the industryProvide general support each fiscal half leading up to earnings and the various investor relations materials that need to be producedProduce key insights to prepare senior leaders for their recurring monthly meetings, as well as periodic meetings with investors, analysts, and the press

Our purpose is crafting iconic drinks chosen for life’s moments. And it’s our people, with their different experiences, perspectives and talents, who make that possible.

We value diversity in its broadest sense and want everyone to feel they can belong, contribute and strive for their personal best. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives — challenging, supporting and learning from one another as one outstanding team.

Together, we’re constantly learning and improving, combining the strength of our people, capabilities and iconic brands to raise the bar, grow and win. Wherever you join us, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, make an impact and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more.

Ready to bring your best? This could be your opportunity.

Overview

Houlihan Lokey, Inc. (NYSE:HLI) is a leading global investment bank recognized for delivering independent strategic and financial advice to corporations, financial sponsors, and governments. With uniquely deep industry expertise, broad international reach, and a partnership approach rooted in trust, the firm provides innovative, integrated solutions across mergers and acquisitions, capital solutions, financial restructuring, and financial and valuation advisory. Our unmatched transaction volumes provide differentiated, data-driven perspectives that help our clients achieve their most critical goals. To learn more about Houlihan Lokey, please visit HL.com.

Financial and Valuation Advisory

Over the past 50+ years, Houlihan Lokey has established one of the largest worldwide financial and valuation advisory practices. Our transaction expertise and leadership in the field of valuation inspire confidence in the financial executives, boards of directors, special committees, investors, and business owners we serve. In 2025, LSEG ranked us the No. 1 global M&A fairness opinion advisor over the past 25 years. Our stability, integrity, technical leadership, and global capabilities make us a trusted advisor for clients worldwide, across a wide range of services, including the Transaction Opinions, Fund Opinions, Transaction Advisory Services, Corporate Valuation Advisory Services, Portfolio Valuation, Real Estate Valuation and Advisory Services, and Dispute Resolution Consulting practices.

Scope:

Within our Portfolio Valuation Complex Securities practice, our clients include many of the world’s largest hedge funds, private equity funds, direct lending funds, business development companies, among other asset managers, and we advise them on the valuations of illiquid debt, equity and complex securities in order to meet their investor and regulatory financial reporting requirements. Our market-leading practice has a strong reputation with regulators, auditors, and investors and we rapidly mobilize the right team for the job, drawing on our expertise in a wide variety of asset classes and industries, along with our firm’s real-world transaction experience and market knowledge.

Financial Analysts within our Portfolio Valuation & Advisory Services practice are fully integrated members of our engagement teams. You will work with a dedicated, highly talented staff of professionals who will give you broad exposure to many issues and concerns affecting businesses today. With a focus in Complex Securities, you will work closely with a smaller and specialized team dedicated in utilizing sophisticated models in valuating securities with complex structure.

We offer a unique opportunity to work on a wealth of projects that provide exposure to various financial and valuation advisory challenges, including the valuation of complex businesses, securities, and transaction structures. As a Financial Analyst, you will research and analyze financial markets data, financial statements, industry conditions and developments, acquisitions and divestitures, and various investment attributes of publicly traded and privately held securities. You will also have an opportunity to develop complex financial models, draft client deliverables, participate in presenting analyses and conclusions, interact with clients on active engagements, and participate in the firm’s marketing efforts.

About Cape

Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data.

Instead of accepting the status quo, we decided to fix it. National security professionals, journalists, parents, and everyone in between can stay connected and have privacy.

We didn’t just build a layer on top of old tech; we built America’s most private and secure mobile carrier from the ground up. By building our own network from scratch, we are able to design and build a suite of privacy and security features that no other carrier on the planet can offer.

Today, Cape provides our secure network to consumers, businesses, and government agencies alike. We closed our Series C in March 2026, and we are scaling rapidly, with the goal of giving people back control of their most personal information.

The Team

At Cape, we are the architects of a privacy-centric movement that is just getting started. We are relentless builders, constantly innovating at the edge of what's possible in telecommunications. We operate on a foundation of high trust and high expectations. Our structure is flat, and collaboration matters more than hierarchy. As a member of our team, you will collaborate with world-class engineers, architects, and visionaries, and work across organizational lines to solve "impossible" problems and deliver mission-critical results for our users every single day.

The Role

Cape Operations Analysts are the high-stakes go-getters who handle our most critical customer touch points. We are Cape's frontline customer success team - technical operators who take on high-volume workflows that impact our privacy-focused Telco business. You will be responsible for managing complex customer interactions and technical troubleshooting, while simultaneously building the operational backend to lead and scale Cape.

We are looking for a detail-oriented, proactive Operations Analyst who is a motivated go-getter and a clear communicator to join our team. Your primary mission is to guarantee customer success, testing the network, confirming reliability, and running down every customer issue until it's resolved. You will be the voice of Cape's customers, closing the loop between the field and our engineers. You'll surface issues, drive fixes, and confirm resolution back with the customer, helping build one of the best-supported networks in the industry. As we grow, you will transition from executing these tasks to building the team and the scalable playbooks that power them.

What You’ll Work On

Build Scalable Solutions: Identify manual bottlenecks in the current process and collaborate with engineering to build automated, more efficient tools. Champion the User: Provide direct input to engineering on trends impacting customers, ensuring our product evolves to meet real-world "in-the-field" needs. Drive Mobile Quality Assurance: Act as a critical internal tester for our mobile applications, identifying bugs and providing feedback to ensure a seamless app experience. Own the Outcome: Learn new operational processes rapidly and take full accountability for their success as Cape scales. Manage Device Inventory & Supply Chain: Serve as a key operator across our device sales shop, confirming compatibility across manufacturers, and managing the flow of hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars in monthly inventory to ensure the right products reach customers. Own Carrier & OEM Relationships: Maintain direct touchpoints with carriers, Google, Apple, and other partners to resolve technical and account issues. Support Fraud Response: Help identify and respond to fraud trends, ensuring Cape's response processes remain coherent and effective. 

Experience

Strong Verbal & Technical Communication: You can lead a technical conversation with engineers and customers with clarity, authority, and empathy. The "Star Player" Mindset: Ability to handle high-volume tasks and multitask across multiple customer issues simultaneously without dropping the ball. Leadership Potential: Experience (or a clear desire) in managing people and workflows; you want to build a team, not just work solo. Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience: Background in business, operations, national service, or a related field (preferred). Prior Experience: Proven track record in a fast-paced operations role, customer support, or executing high-volume technical tasks. Bonus Points:Experience with supply chain, logistics, eCommerce, or telecommunications workflows. Experience with basic product quality assurance, specifically mobile app testing and bug trackingFamiliarity with mobile device troubleshooting, command line, radio communications, or other technical flows. 
Compensation

We offer competitive compensation that is geo-adjusted based on your location, along with meaningful equity so you share in the value you help create. Salary range for this role in New York, NY or Arlington, VA is $100,000-$110,000 depending on experience and interview performance.

Our benefits include:

401(k) match100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your dependents12 weeks paid parental leave (for all parents, no waiting period)Stipends forFamily-forming needsGender-affirming careUnlimited PTO

Our Culture & Values

We hire excellent people, give them outsized responsibility, and trust them to execute. Every person at Cape has a proven track record of tackling hard problems and winning. We believe that personal privacy and national security are not at odds, and that they can be reconciled through strong technology. We believe companies exist to build awesome things and take care of the people who build them, so we offer top-tier healthcare, 401(k) matching, and a generous vacation policy that our team actually uses to recharge. We believe that a stronger company and a better product are built by people from all walks of life. We hire without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, disability, or Veteran status. If you are great at what you do, you belong here.

CONTRACT TITLE

Research Assistant

FLSA

Non-exempt

CAMPUS SPECIFIC INFORMATION

The Graduate Center of the City University of New York (CUNY) is the focal point for advanced teaching and research at CUNY, the nation's largest urban public university. With over 35 doctoral and master's programs of the highest caliber, the Graduate Center fosters pioneering research and scholarship in the arts and sciences and prepares students for careers in universities and the private, nonprofit, and government sectors. The Graduate Center's commitment to research and scholarship for the public good is exemplified by its more than 30 centers, institutes, and initiatives, including its Advanced Science Research Center (ASRC), a 200,000 square-foot facility in upper Manhattan, designed to promote collaboration among scientists in five areas of global research and innovation: nanoscience, photonics, structural biology, neuroscience, and environmental sciences.

The Graduate Center (GC) benefits from highly ambitious and diverse students and alumni-who in turn teach hundreds of thousands of undergraduates every year. Through its public programs, the Graduate Center enhances New York City's intellectual and cultural life.

A Research Assistant position is available in the laboratory of Dr. J. Wren Kim at the Neuroscience Initiative of the Advanced Science Research Center (ASRC).

Our laboratory seeks to understand the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal adaptation to changing environments and how these processes contribute to brain function and dysfunction. Using innovative high-throughput approaches, we investigate how neurons regulate gene expression to maintain homeostatic control of neuronal network activity.

The laboratory is embedded within the vibrant and multidisciplinary research environment of the ASRC Neuroscience Initiative, where multiple research groups share laboratory space, resources, and expertise. We strongly value collaboration, the open exchange of ideas, and interdisciplinary approaches to scientific discovery. The ASRC provides access to state-of-the-art facilities, advanced instrumentation, and dedicated scientific support staff, creating an exceptional environment for training and research.

This position requires the incumbent to work in the lab Monday-Friday.

Research (75%):

 Conduct independent and collaborative research experiments under the supervision of the Principal Investigator (PI). Apply techniques in biochemistry, cell biology, molecular biology, and related disciplines. Perform cell culture, molecular cloning, protein and nucleic acid analyses, and other experimental procedures as required. Maintain accurate and detailed records of experimental procedures, data, and findings.

Laboratory Support (25%):

 Assist the PI with managing laboratory inventory, including ordering and tracking reagents, consumables, and equipment. Assist with preventative maintenance and repairs of lab equipment as needed. Assist with onboarding and training of new laboratory members on standard procedures. Maintain laboratory organization and ensure compliance with institutional safety regulations. Adhere to standards for safety and hygiene and ethical conduct as defined by the University and relevant outside parties. Perform related duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience relevant to the research being performed.

Preferred Qualifications:

 Prior laboratory research experience in molecular and cellular biology is essential. Experience working with rodents. Flexibility in work schedule to accommodate experimental needs. Willingnessto work both independently and collaboratively in a research environment. Interest in contributing to a dynamic and multidisciplinary research program.

Clinical Research Coordinators (CRCs) are key members of research teams at Columbia University Irving Medical Center (CUIMC). Key responsibilities include study coordination, data collection, regulatory compliance, and serving as a research liaison. The ideal candidate has strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills; a background in research or health administration is a plus, but not a requirement.

This Clinical Research Coordinator I position will support the division of movement disorders clinical research core within the department of Neurology. The candidate will report to the senior clinical research manager and will assist in executing a broad portfolio of movement disorders research initiatives, including gene therapy, stem cell therapy, biomarker, and observational studies spanning Parkinson’s disease, essential tremor, multiple system atrophy, spinocerebellar ataxia, and other movement disorders and neurodegenerative conditions.

Position Summary

The Columbia Center for Translational Immunology (CCTI) at Columbia University Irving Medical Center (CUIMC) seeks a highly motivated and talented Clinical Research Coordinator to join its research team. The Coordinator will support laboratory and clinical research studies involving transplant recipients and humanized mouse models generated using patient-derived bone marrow stem cells.

Primary responsibilities include data collection and analysis before and after organ transplantation, maintenance of Institutional Review Board (IRB) protocols, coordination of specimen collection and processing, database management, and support of translational immunology research initiatives. Working within CCTI, the Coordinator will recruit and enroll study participants, coordinate specimen collection and processing, obtain and compile HLA typing data, and assist with the development and analysis of human immune system mouse models.

The Coordinator will report to the Laboratory Director and will maintain specimen inventories, manage sample distribution to laboratory personnel, and support biobanking operations. The successful candidate must possess strong organizational and interpersonal skills, a solid understanding of basic laboratory techniques, exceptional attention to detail, and a demonstrated commitment to scientific integrity and professional excellence.

Responsibilities

Process and manage human biological specimens.Maintain accurate specimen records and databases.Order laboratory supplies and manage inventory levels.Monitor, maintain, and coordinate servicing of laboratory equipment.Assist with billing and invoicing for Biobank services.Collaborate with investigators, the Scientific Review Committee (SRC), and Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) to ensure compliance with study protocols and regulatory requirements.Obtain, process, and store fetal tissue in accordance with study protocols and applicable federal, state, institutional, and laboratory policies.Participate in clinical research studies involving transplantation.Recruit, enroll, and follow study participants; assist with human sample processing and data analysis.Process and ship blood, lymphoid tissue, intestinal tissue, bone marrow, and stool specimens in accordance with sponsor protocols and applicable federal, state, and institutional regulations.Isolate genomic DNA (gDNA) from collected specimens and coordinate HLA typing and single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) analyses.Compile, analyze, and disseminate HLA typing results for donors and transplant recipients.Collect, manage, and analyze clinical data from EPIC electronic medical records and the UNOS donor database, including demographic information, HLA typing, immunosuppression regimens, episodes of rejection and infection, donor-specific antibody (DSA) development, and other clinical outcomes.Participate in Human Studies Core projects and interlaboratory collaborative studies.Maintain protocol-specific regulatory documents, study files, and research records; enter and manage study data within centralized and study-specific databases.Attend and actively participate in laboratory meetings, data monitoring meetings, and scientific seminars; provide updates on recruitment, study progress, and research activities.Report to the Principal Investigator and Laboratory Director within CCTI and the Department of Medicine.Prepare, submit, and maintain IRB protocols, amendments, continuing reviews, and related regulatory documentation.Process invoices and assist with financial reconciliation activities for the Human Studies Core.Perform additional duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Immunology, Biology, Life Sciences, Public Health, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.Excellent interpersonal, written, verbal, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with clinical populations and multidisciplinary teams.Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex tasks while exercising sound judgment and adhering to all federal, state, institutional, and departmental regulations and guidelines.Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within research and clinical environments.Commitment to a minimum two-year term in the position.

Preferred Qualifications

New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) is the State’s affordable housing agency, with a mission to build, preserve, and protect affordable housing and increase homeownership throughout New York State.

Our work would not be possible without the diverse backgrounds, experiences, ideas, and abilities of our employees. Resilient Homes and Communities (RHC) now serves as the lead principal office responsible for the administration of New York State’s multiple CDBG-DR awards. RHC operates within the New York State Housing Trust Fund Corporation (HTFC) and the Homeownership and Community Development (HOCD) unit, which consists of the State of New York Mortgage Agency, the Affordable Housing Corporation, the Office of Community Renewal, the Office of Special Initiatives and RHC.
Position Summary
The Data Analyst will play a key supporting role analyzing, visualizing and reporting data for the Office of Resilient Homes and Communities. This position combines data science, spatial data analysis (GIS) with business and policy research to support reporting, decision-making, and program quality across the agency. Reporting to the Director of Research and Data, the Data Analyst will assist in maintaining spatial and quantitative databases, updating the federal Disaster Recovery Grants Reporting (DRGR) system, and producing maps, dashboards, and reports. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career professional to gain hands-on experience in disaster recovery policy, data integrity, and public sector data analysis.
Duties and Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

 Data & Reporting Support: Assist in the development, update, and maintenance of performance management reports, dashboards, and ad hoc data analyses to support program operations.
 GIS & Spatial Analysis: Support program teams by maintaining Esri ArcGIS software/ArcGIS Online platforms, performing basic spatial analyses, and creating maps and graphs for internal and external stakeholders.
 System Maintenance: Help input, track, and verify service areas and program data within New York State’s internal systems and the federal Disaster Recovery Grant Reporting (DRGR) system to ensure accuracy across program records.
 Data Quality & Documentation: Assist in documenting data methodologies, maintaining Standards of Procedure (SOPs) for federal reporting, and performing routine data cleaning and quality control.
 Research Assistance: Provide analytical and research support for ongoing projects evaluating the impact of RHC programs on New York State residents.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with internal program teams and external partners to share, transfer, and package data for reporting and research needs.

Qualifications:

 Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Geography, Urban Planning, Public Policy, Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field*
 Knowledge of public policy in areas such as disaster recovery, infrastructure, housing, economic development, and/or resiliency is preferred.
 Experience distilling quantitative and qualitative policy analysis into written descriptions such as briefs, memos, etc.
 2 years professional experience in an analytic role*
 Demonstrated experience using Esri ArcGIS 10.x, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Server, Model Builder, R and basic python programming. 
 Excellent oral, written, and quantitative skills.
 Exceptional problem-solving abilities. 
 Exceptional ability to use data to make decisions. 
 Expertise in the use of Microsoft Office products, specifically Excel and Access.
 Ability to work in a flexible, fast paced, mission driven environment.

*Substitutions: four years of specialized experience or associate’s degree and two years of specialized experience may substitute for bachelor’s degree; J.D. or master’s degree may substitute for one year of specialized experience; Ph.D. may substitute for two years of specialized experience.
This job description is not intended to be all inclusive and the employee will be expected to perform other reasonably related duties as assigned.
APPLICANTS MUST INCLUDE A RESUME
WHAT WE OFFER AT NYS HCR: 

 Extensive benefits package including participation in New York State’s Health Insurance Program and New York State & Local Employees’ Retirement System.
 Promotional opportunities for dedicated professionals.
 Work-life balance benefits including a 37.5-hour work week, opportunity for compressed scheduling, and paid time off benefits (vacation, sick, personal days, and federal holidays).
 12 weeks of Paid Parental Leave.

The PSLF Program forgives the remaining balance on your Direct Loans after you have made 120 qualifying monthly payments under an accepted repayment plan and while working full-time for an eligible employer.

Under the leadership of Governor Kathy Hochul and Commissioner RuthAnne Visnauskas, HCR is a vibrant, innovative agency that integrates and leverages New York State’s housing resources. We have offices in New York City, Albany, Buffalo, and Syracuse, and employ a diverse workforce of professionals who are hard-working and committed to serving low- and moderate-income families. As an Applied AI Engineer at SOCOTEC, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and deploying AI models that enhance our chatbot program and other AI-driven solutions. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, including data scientists, software engineers, and business stakeholders, to integrate advanced AI technologies that address real-world challenges within our industry. Developing AI Models: Design and implement machine learning models tailored to natural language processing (NLP) and other AI applications within our chatbot and enterprise systems. Collaborating with Cross-Functional Teams: Work closely with product managers, data scientists, and software engineers to translate business requirements into intelligent AI-driven solutions. Building and Maintaining AI Pipelines: Create and optimize end-to-end machine learning pipelines, from data preprocessing to model deployment, ensuring scalability and performance. Optimizing Model Performance: Continuously fine-tune and improve the accuracy, speed, and robustness of AI models, leveraging techniques like hyperparameter tuning and model optimization. Integrating AI Solutions: Work closely with backend engineers to integrate AI models into production environments using tools like LangChain and cloud services. Staying Updated with AI/ML Trends: Keep up with the latest developments in AI, machine learning, and natural language processing, applying new techniques to improve our technology stack. Documentation: Provide detailed documentation of AI workflows, models, and algorithms to facilitate collaboration and ensure long-term maintainability. Perform all duties as assigned by your manager

Qualifications

Proficiency in Python and experience with AI/ML libraries such as Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and Hugging Face. Strong understanding of natural language processing (NLP) and experience building chatbot or conversational AI systems. Hands-on experience with AI model development, including data preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and deployment. Familiarity with AI/ML tools like Jupyter Notebook and cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure. Experience with version control systems (e.g., Git, GitHub) and agile development methodologies. Ability to optimize model performance and scale AI solutions for production use. Experience with frameworks like LangChain for building conversational AI workflows. Experience with containerization tools like Docker for deploying AI solutions. Passion for exploring and implementing the latest advancements in AI technology.

For more information, please visit www.socotec.us

rows.title: Robot Learning - Founding Engineer
rows.descriptionText:
Location: Brooklyn, NY, at Newlab · In person · Full-time
About ElenchElench builds autonomous factories. We build the factory and deploy the robots that run it. Our current focus is automating the 3D printing of a real product (toolbox.shop) and the tasks around it (e.g., swapping build plates and packing orders).Running generic tasks in a factory requires a generic robot platform. That's why we're building a wheeled humanoid robot, trained with VLA models on demonstrations from our own factory. We'll then sell it as a battle-tested robot that performs tasks in our customers' factories, such as machine tending, picking, packing and assembly.Elench was founded by Alex Plugaru, co-founder and former CTO of Gorgias, who scaled the company from $0 to $90M ARR.
What it's like hereWe're early, and going from a prototype to something that works is a lot of work. You'll be one of the first engineers, working directly with the founder. Expect to bootstrap the training lifecycle: data collection, cleanup and fine-tuning. If you want a finished platform and a narrow job, this isn't it. If you want to own a large part of a robot that does real work, this is for you.
The roleYou'll be our founding robot learning engineer. You own how the robot learns: from a person demonstrating a task to a skill the robot runs on its own, measured over many trials. You'll work on a small fleet of robots that collect data every day, with the founder and our hardware engineer next to you.
What you'll doGet the robot's first skills working: packing customer orders (folding a mailer, placing items, sealing, labeling) and swapping build plates on 3D printers.Fine-tune open VLA models, starting with π0.5, on our data, and run them on the robot.Decide what data we collect: write the procedures our teleoperators follow, review their recordings, and choose what to record next from where the policy fails.Define what success means for each skill, and measure it over many real trials before calling the skill done.Improve our teleoperation and recording tools where they slow down data collection or hurt data quality.Help with the hardware: cameras, grippers, arms. If something breaks during a run, you help fix it.
Who you areYou've trained a manipulation policy and run it on a real robot, and you know its success rate.You care more about the robot working than about the method being new.You'd rather be in the lab next to the robot than only in front of a screen.You do your best work with a lot of trust and little process.
Experience and skillsImitation learning or VLA fine-tuning on real robots: ACT, diffusion policy, π0/π0.5, GR00T or similarTeleoperated data collection, and a feel for what makes demonstrations train well (LeRobot or similar)Python and PyTorch, Linux, GPUsDebugging across the stack: a dropped camera frame, a CAN error, a broken datasetNice to have: two-armed robots, dora or ROS 2, JAX, simulation for evaluationThis role is about making a robot work in production. If your main goal is pretraining foundation models or publishing papers, it isn't a fit.
Compensation$170,000–$200,000 base salary, plus equity and benefits.
How to applySend your CV and a robot you trained, as a video plus its success rate over a number of trials, to alex@elench.com. Finalists do a paid trial week on our robots.

rows.title: Postdoctoral Research Scientist Breast Cancer Metastasis and Tumor Microenvironment
rows.descriptionText:
A postdoctoral position is available in the Entenberg laboratory at Albert Einstein College of Medicine to study mechanisms regulating breast cancer dissemination, metastatic progression, and recurrence.
We are looking for an enthusiastic, organized, and highly motivated individual to join a multidisciplinary team of cancer biologists, biomedical engineers, imaging scientists, and physician-scientists. The research integrates cancer biology with advanced imaging, microfluidics, engineered cell-based systems, and mouse models to investigate how physical and cellular features of the tumor microenvironment influence cancer-cell behavior.
The fellow will contribute to several newly funded projects examining cancer-cell stemness and mechanotransduction, tumor-cell re-dissemination from established metastatic lesions, and the role of macrophage populations in local and distant recurrence from early-stage breast cancer lesions. Experimental approaches include fluorescent reporters and biosensors, engineered cell-based assays, mouse models of breast cancer, photoconversion/photoactivation, microfluidics, and intravital multiphoton microscopy.
This position offers a unique opportunity for truly interdisciplinary training across cancer biology, advanced imaging, microfluidics, and quantitative experimental approaches. Fellows with a strong cancer biology background will gain expertise in advanced imaging and microfluidic approaches, while those with stronger technical training will deepen their understanding of cancer metastasis, tumor microenvironment biology, and in vivo experimental models.
Applicants should have, or be about to complete, a PhD or MD, or equivalent doctoral degree in cancer biology, cell biology, biomedical engineering, biophysics, or a closely related field. Experience in cancer metastasis, tumor microenvironment or macrophage biology, mammalian cell culture, mouse models, fluorescence microscopy, mechanobiology, or advanced cell-based assays would be particularly valuable.We are especially interested in candidates who are comfortable working with advanced experimental technologies, enjoy troubleshooting complex systems, and are able to learn and apply new techniques quickly. Candidates should be willing to work with live mice and have a strong interest in learning and applying microfluidics, intravital microscopy, and other advanced imaging approaches. First author publications and excellent experimental design, communication, and collaborative skills are required, as is the ability to work independently in a team setting.
To apply, please send a CV, a brief statement describing prior research and research interests, and contact information for three references to: David Entenberg: david.entenberg@einsteinmed.edu (https://einsteinmed.edu/faculty/10605/david-entenberg/)
Albert Einstein College of Medicine. Einstein is an equal opportunity employer.Position Location: Bronx, New YorkApplication Deadline: Open until filled
Salary Range: $70,000-$75,000

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
Employment Type: Full-timeWork Setting: In-office or remoteWork Location: New York (in-office) or remote USWork Hours: Office hoursFind out more here: https://www.citrini.com/
Position OverviewCitrini Research is looking for a robotics analyst to help cover one of the most important emerging themes in markets: the move from software-only AI into physical AI, automation, humanoids, industrial robotics, and the supply chains behind them.We are not looking for a narrow technical specialist or someone with a decade of industry experience. We are looking for someone early in their career who is intensely curious, high-energy, analytical, and willing to learn fast.The job is to figure out what matters, who matters, and where the investable opportunities are. That means tracking companies, products, deployments, suppliers, customers, technical milestones, and market narratives, then turning that work into clear research.A robotics background is helpful. A finance background is helpful. Neither is strictly required. What matters most is judgment, curiosity, writing ability, and the ability to chase a topic until you actually understand it.
ResponsibilitiesResearch robotics, humanoids, automation, physical AI, industrial technology, and related supply chains.Track companies, product launches, factory deployments, partnerships, funding rounds, customer announcements, and supplier relationships.Build simple but useful datasets on robotics companies, components, deployments, revenue exposure, and market size.Identify public companies that may benefit from robotics growth, including suppliers, manufacturers, software companies, semiconductor vendors, and industrial automation businesses.Read filings, earnings transcripts, investor decks, technical papers, patents, product materials, and industry commentary.Speak with industry experts, operators, engineers, investors, suppliers, and customers.Write research notes and longer thematic reports for investors.Help separate real technical or commercial progress from hype.
Requirements1-4 years of professional experience preferred, but will consider recent graduates.Strong interest in robotics, AI, automation, manufacturing, engineering, industrial technology, or public markets.Ability to learn technical subjects quickly and explain them clearly.Strong writing skills.Strong analytical instincts and attention to detail.Comfortable working independently and figuring things out without a fixed playbook.Willingness to dig through messy sources, obscure companies, filings, presentations, transcripts, and technical materials.High curiosity, high output, and low ego.
Helpful BackgroundsRobotics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, industrial engineering, or related coursework.Equity research, investing, consulting, banking, journalism, corporate strategy, or industry research.Experience with robotics clubs, engineering projects, labs, startups, internships, competitions, or technical writing.Comfort with Excel or basic data analysis.Python, SQL, CAD, simulation, or other technical tools are a plus, but not required.Existing writing, research, projects, GitHub work, blog posts, investment memos, or technical breakdowns.
What We Are Not Looking ForSomeone who needs a perfectly defined assignment before starting.Someone who summarizes what others have already said.Someone who is purely academic and uninterested in business or markets.Someone who mistakes complexity for insight.
Growth AreasHelp build Citrini’s robotics and physical AI coverage from an early stage.Develop expertise across humanoids, automation, actuators, sensors, machine vision, simulation, manufacturing, and robotics supply chains.Learn how to turn technical research into investment conclusions.Build relationships with founders, engineers, operators, suppliers, and investors.Publish work read by professional investors and allocators.

rows.descriptionText:
DRW is a diversified trading firm with over 3 decades of experience bringing sophisticated technology and exceptional people together to operate in markets around the world. We value autonomy and the ability to quickly pivot to capture opportunities, so we operate using our own capital and trading at our own risk.

Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

We operate with respect, curiosity and open minds. The people who thrive here share our belief that it’s not just what we do that matters–it's how we do it. DRW is a place of high expectations, integrity, innovation and a willingness to challenge consensus.

DRW is looking for a Quantitative Researcher to join our growing Prediction Markets team. The team develops systematic trading strategies across a wide range of prediction markets. This role combines quantitative modeling, market data analysis, and strategy development to identify opportunities in rapidly evolving markets. You will work closely with traders and engineers across the full strategy lifecycle, from initial research and model development through production deployment and live performance analysis.

What You’ll Do

Apply statistical and machine learning methods to develop predictive models and trading signalsAnalyze large and diverse datasets to identify market opportunities and inefficienciesResearch how short-term signals from related financial markets can improve prediction-market pricing and tradingConduct research into pricing, market making, market microstructure, execution, and risk managementConduct rigorous quantitative research and evaluate strategies through backtesting and simulationDevelop analytical tools to monitor performance and improve live strategiesCollaborate with traders and engineers to translate successful research into production trading systemsExplore new products, datasets, and approaches as the prediction-markets business expands

What We’re Looking For

2+ years of experience in quantitative research, systematic trading, data science, or a related fieldDegree in a quantitative or technical discipline such as mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, physics, or economicsStrong knowledge of probability, statistics, and quantitative modelingExperience conducting research with large, noisy, real-world datasetsStrong programming skills, particularly in PythonAbility to formulate and independently drive open-ended research problemsStrong attention to detail and a rigorous approach to testing and validating resultsAbility to communicate complex ideas clearly and work effectively with traders, researchers, and engineersIntellectual curiosity and a genuine interest in financial markets and prediction markets

Additional Experience That Would Be Helpful

Systematic or electronic tradingHigh-frequency or short-horizon signal researchProbabilistic forecasting or machine learningStrategy backtesting and performance analysisExperience moving quantitative research into live production

The strongest candidates will combine quantitative rigor with practical judgment, intellectual curiosity, and a willingness to take ownership of difficult, open-ended problems.

The annual base salary range for this position is $200,000 to $300,000 depending on the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and relevant skill set. The position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. In addition, DRW offers a comprehensive suite of employee benefits including group medical, pharmacy, dental and vision insurance, 401k (with discretionary employer match), short and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, health savings accounts, and flexible spending accounts.

SOCOTEC’s combination of expertise, experience and methods are increasingly recognized as best-in-class fueling significant growth.

Job Description

As an Applied AI Engineer at SOCOTEC, you will be responsible for designing, developing, and deploying AI models that enhance our chatbot program and other AI-driven solutions. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, including data scientists, software engineers, and business stakeholders, to integrate advanced AI technologies that address real-world challenges within our industry. You will focus on building scalable, efficient, and accurate machine learning pipelines while staying at the forefront of the latest AI advancements.

Developing AI Models: Design and implement machine learning models tailored to natural language processing (NLP) and other AI applications within our chatbot and enterprise systems. Collaborating with Cross-Functional Teams: Work closely with product managers, data scientists, and software engineers to translate business requirements into intelligent AI-driven solutions. Building and Maintaining AI Pipelines: Create and optimize end-to-end machine learning pipelines, from data preprocessing to model deployment, ensuring scalability and performance. Optimizing Model Performance: Continuously fine-tune and improve the accuracy, speed, and robustness of AI models, leveraging techniques like hyperparameter tuning and model optimization. Implementing Best Practices in AI/ML Development: Ensure the reliability and quality of AI models by following best practices for training, testing, and model evaluation. Integrating AI Solutions: Work closely with backend engineers to integrate AI models into production environments using tools like LangChain and cloud services. Staying Updated with AI/ML Trends: Keep up with the latest developments in AI, machine learning, and natural language processing, applying new techniques to improve our technology stack. Documentation: Provide detailed documentation of AI workflows, models, and algorithms to facilitate collaboration and ensure long-term maintainability. Perform all duties as assigned by your manager

Qualifications

Proficiency in Python and experience with AI/ML libraries such as Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and Hugging Face. Strong understanding of natural language processing (NLP) and experience building chatbot or conversational AI systems. Hands-on experience with AI model development, including data preprocessing, model training, evaluation, and deployment. Familiarity with AI/ML tools like Jupyter Notebook and cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure. Experience with version control systems (e.g., Git, GitHub) and agile development methodologies. Ability to optimize model performance and scale AI solutions for production use. Experience with frameworks like LangChain for building conversational AI workflows. The ideal candidate should have at least 4-7 years of experience

Familiarity with reinforcement learning, transfer learning, or other advanced AI techniques. Knowledge of model monitoring, A/B testing, and continuous improvement strategies for AI systems. Experience with containerization tools like Docker for deploying AI solutions. Passion for exploring and implementing the latest advancements in AI technology. 

We are seeking a creative and detail-oriented individual who is passionate about building and deploying AI-driven solutions. If you thrive in a collaborative environment and are excited about shaping the future of AI at SOCOTEC, we encourage you to apply.

Additional Information

For more information, please visit www.socotec.us

Salary: $157-200k

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

As a Commercial Due Diligence Consultant, you’ll focus on buy‑side and sell‑side transaction engagements, supporting corporate clients and private equity investors as they evaluate growth opportunities, revenue sustainability, and market risk. You’ll work alongside experienced professionals across Grant Thornton | Stax Transactions to deliver clear, data‑driven insights throughout the transaction lifecycle.

From day one, you’ll be empowered to make an impact—helping clients make confident investment decisions while continuing to build your leadership and advisory skillset.

 Support commercial due diligence engagements for corporate and private‑equity‑backed transactions  Analyze markets, customers, competitors, pricing, and go‑to‑market strategies to assess commercial risk and opportunity  Conduct market sizing, growth forecasting, customer segmentation, and demand analyses  Prepare clear, concise, and investment‑committee‑ready findings summarizing key risks and value drivers  Draft diligence reports, executive summaries, and presentation materials  Collaborate with Financial Due Diligence, Value Creation, IT, and Human Capital teams to deliver integrated transaction insights  Other duties as assigned 

Required

 You have the following technical skills, qualifications, and abilities: 

 Bachelor’s degree in business, Economics, Finance, Strategy, or a related field  Typically, 2–4+ years of experience in commercial due diligence, strategy consulting, transaction advisory, or private equity‑related roles  Experience supporting M&A or private equity transactions  Strong analytical skills across market sizing, customer analysis, and competitive dynamics  Ability to synthesize complex data into clear, actionable insights  Excellent written, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills  Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast‑paced, transaction‑oriented environment 

Preferred

 Experience working directly with private equity clients  Consulting or professional services background  MBA or other advanced degree 

Locations:

 Chicago, Boston, and NYC.  Consistent with the firm’s hybrid work model, this position requires in-person attendance three days per week at a firm office or client site. 

Compensation & Benefits

This role offers competitive compensation, including a base salary range of $115,000–$140,000, plus a target annual bonus. Grant Thornton Stax follows a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy, base salary is commensurate with experience, and total cash compensation may vary based on individual and firm performance.

We also offer a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family; expanded family planning benefits; a 401(k) plan with company contributions regardless of your own; open vacation policy; life and disability insurance; generous parental leave; pre-tax transit benefits; mobile phone stipend; wellness reimbursement; charitable gift matching; and more.

Grant Thornton Stax is an equal opportunity employer and affords equal opportunity to all applicants for all positions without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability (except where the disability is a bona fide occupational disqualification), sexual orientation, genetic makeup, predisposition or carrier status, familial or marital status, military or veteran status or any other status protected under local, state or federal laws.

rows.title: Technical Product Marketing Manager
rows.descriptionText:
About UsWe're ClosedWon Talent, a sales and go-to-market recruiting agency that specializes in working with fast-growing startups. If you're exploring your next move, we might have just the opportunity for you, including this one.
About the StartupOur client is a well-funded Series A startup building a test orchestration platform for engineering and QA teams working in modern cloud and Kubernetes environments. Rather than asking teams to rip out the testing tools they already use, the platform sits alongside them, letting teams run tests written in any language or framework and giving engineering leaders full visibility into what's running across the organization and where things are failing. They recently launched an AI-powered feature that writes and runs tests from a plain-English prompt, they sell to companies of every size from growing startups to large enterprises, and their customers tend to expand quickly once they're on board, with retention in the high 90s. The company is targeting 3x growth next year and is investing heavily in marketing to get there.
About the RoleThis is a technical product marketing role designed for someone who loves the parts of solutions engineering that involve teaching, demoing, and creating, and wants to do more of that without being tied to individual accounts. You'll join a six-person marketing team and report to a marketing leader who made this same transition himself, moving from solutions engineering into product marketing, so you'll be coached on the marketing side by someone who understands exactly where you're coming from.
Most of your time will go toward creating technical content and assets for customers and the broader engineering audience, including demos, demo environments, technical blogs, architecture explainers, walkthroughs, and best-practice guides. The rest will go toward supporting product launches from messaging through rollout, building enablement materials that help the sales team sell (battlecards, objection handling, demo guidance, and one-pagers), turning customer stories into case studies and proof points, and keeping an eye on the competitive landscape. You'll work closely with product, engineering, sales, and marketing, and you'll have plenty of opportunities to get in front of audiences through webinars, videos, and live demos at events.
Need-to-HaveRoughly 3–5 years of experience in a technical, customer-facing role at a technology company, such as solutions engineering, sales engineering, technical account management, developer relations, or client-facing product management.Hands-on experience demoing a technical software product to customers or prospects, along with the ability to explain complex concepts clearly and patiently to both technical and non-technical audiences.Genuine curiosity about how products work and a willingness to learn by getting your hands dirty in the product.A real interest in creating content, presenting, and educating audiences, and a desire to move toward marketing as the next step in your career.Strong writing and project management skills.Based in the Boston area and interested in working in a hybrid work environment
Nice-to-HaveExperience with developer tools, DevOps, automated testing, CI/CD, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, or cybersecurity.Prior exposure to product marketing, product launches, sales enablement, or customer marketing, although this isn't required and the hiring manager is happy to teach it.Experience as a developer advocate, evangelist, or technical CSM focused on customer education and advocacy.A track record of creating content such as demo videos, how-to guides, webinars, or conference presentations.That instinct for knowing what a customer needs to see before the sales conversation even starts.
