rows.descriptionText:
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, wealth management and investment management services.

About Parametric

Parametric is part of Morgan Stanley Investment Management, the asset management division of Morgan Stanley. We partner with advisors, institutions, and consultants to build portfolios focused on what's important to them and their clients. A leader in custom solutions for more than 30 years, we help investors access efficient market exposures, solve implementation challenges, and design multi-asset portfolios that respond to their evolving needs. We also offer systematic alpha and alternative strategies to complement clients' core holdings. Learn more here: https://www.parametricportfolio.com/about

This role is part of Parametric’ s hybrid working model, which includes working in the office 3 days a week and choosing to work remotely or in the office the remaining days of the week.

Office Locations: Seattle, Boston, Minneapolis and Alpharetta, GA

Excellent opportunity for recent or soon to be 2027 graduates! Office Locations: Seattle, Boston, Minneapolis, Alpharetta

SUMMER COHORT STARTS - July 2027

About The Operations Analyst Program

The Operations Analyst Program is an early-career development opportunity for driven recent and soon-to-be graduates who want to launch a career at the intersection of investment management, operations, data, and technology. Analysts use analytical, technical, and collaborative skills to help deliver operational excellence, solve business challenges, and improve outcomes for clients.

As investment operations evolve through data, automation, and AI, analysts gain hands-on experience supporting business-critical investment processes while helping identify opportunities to improve how work gets done. Through ownership of operational processes and exposure to continuous improvement, data analytics, automation, workflow design, and AI, analysts strengthen controls, improve decision-making, and contribute to scalable solutions that support clients and business growth.

Over three weeks, Analysts begin as a cohort with an immersion in Parametric's investment strategies, operating model, and Operations organization. Following onboarding, analysts join teams supporting Market, Client, or Control functions, where they develop domain expertise, learn business-critical workflows, and build an end-to-end understanding of how Operations supports clients, portfolios, risk management, and business growth.

Operations teams are responsible for the execution, oversight, servicing, and control activities that support the investment lifecycle. Analysts work closely with teammates and stakeholders across the organization to execute processes accurately, resolve operational challenges, improve controls, and deliver exceptional client outcomes.

In addition to their core team responsibilities, analysts may collaborate with specialized teams within Operations focused on process transformation, analytics, workflow modernization, automation, and AI-enabled solutions. Partnering with subject matter experts across Market, Client, and Control functions to identify opportunities, redesign processes, and implement scalable improvements that enhance operational effectiveness. Through this partnership, analysts may gain exposure to transformation initiatives while continuing to build deep operational expertise.

The program is designed for people who are curious about how businesses operate, motivated to improve processes, and eager to continue learning. As business needs evolve, analysts may gain exposure to different Operations functions, participate in cross-functional initiatives, or contribute to transformation efforts, broadening their knowledge, experience, and skill sets.

What You'll Do And Learn

Learn Parametric's investment strategies, operating model, and business-critical Operations workflows, and understand how Market, Client, and Control functions support clients, portfolios, risk management, and business growth.Learn and execute business-critical investment operations workflows accurately and on time. Responsibilities may include activities such as cash and position reconciliation, trade lifecycle support, client servicing, corporate actions, account onboarding and maintenance, contracts, oversight activities, and billing, depending on team assignment.Develop an end-to-end understanding of assigned processes, including activities, decisions, systems, data flows, controls, handoffs, and upstream and downstream dependencies.Investigate exceptions, breaks, recurring operational issues, and client-impacting events using structured problem-solving and data analysis. Identify root causes, assess impacts, and recommend sustainable solutions.Partner with Operations teams, portfolio managers, traders, sales, product management, technology teams, external providers, and other stakeholders to resolve issues, improve handoffs, and support business priorities.Perform quality control and verification activities, maintain accurate records and documentation, and help ensure operational processes meet established policies, procedures, and control standards.Analyze operational and investment data to identify patterns, anomalies, trends, bottlenecks, and emerging risks. Build reports, dashboards, or analytical tools that turn data into actionable insights and improvement opportunities.Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, or redesign workflows and contribute to process mapping, requirements gathering, testing, implementation, and adoption activities.Collaborate with Automation, Reinvention & Collaboration (ARC) and other partners on process-improvement initiatives, workflow modernization efforts, analytics projects, automation solutions, and AI-enabled capabilities.Use or learn tools such as Excel, Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI, SQL, Python, workflow automation platforms, process-modeling tools, and approved AI solutions, as appropriate to the assignment.Contribute to operational excellence, analytics, automation, or process-improvement initiatives and present findings, recommendations, and outcomes to team members and business partners.

What You'll Bring

Associate or bachelor's degree completed by the program start date. Relevant fields may include industrial, process, or systems engineering; operations research; supply chain; data science or analytics; computer science; information systems; mathematics; statistics; finance; accounting; economics; or a related analytical, business, or technical field. Candidates from other majors with relevant quantitative, technical, or process-improvement experience are also encouraged to apply.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to break down ambiguous issues, work with data, identify root causes, and form well-supported conclusions.A systems-thinking and continuous-improvement mindset, including curiosity about how people, processes, data, controls, and technology interact end to end and a desire to make work simpler, more accurate, efficient, scalable, and controlled.High attention to detail and a commitment to quality, sound judgment, risk awareness, responsible use of data and technology, and positive client outcomes.Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with teammates and stakeholders and communicate complex ideas in a clear and organized manner.Ownership, learning agility, adaptability, and the ability to prioritize effectively in a collaborative, deadline-driven environment.Experience using spreadsheets to organize and analyze information and communicate findings, or the ability to learn quickly.Strong interest in building a career at the intersection of investment management, operations, process improvement, data, and technology.Ability to work full-time (40 hours per week) by the program start date.

Preferred Qualifications

Coursework, internships, or project experience involving process mapping, continuous improvement, business analysis, data analysis, automation, workflow design, programming, analytics, or AI.Exposure to one or more tools such as Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI, SQL, Python, workflow automation platforms, process-modeling tools, version control platforms, or similar technologies.Familiarity with financial markets, investment management, or business operations. Prior investment operations experience is not required.Experience contributing to a cross-functional project, presenting recommendations, developing a prototype, or helping others adopt a new process, workflow, or technology solution.

rows.descriptionText:
About Cedar Gate Technologies

Cedar Gate Technologies, an IQVIA business, enables payers, providers, employers, and service administrators to excel at value-based care with a unified technology and services platform delivering analytics, care, and payment technology on a single data management foundation. At Cedar Gate, you’ll be part of a collaborative, innovative environment where great ideas thrive. We invest deeply in our people through ongoing training, comprehensive benefits, and a strong culture of teamwork, offering the chance to grow your skills while contributing to high impact initiatives for some of the world's most dynamic companies.

Position Summary

At Cedar Gate Technologies, an IQVIA business, our Data Onboarding Analysts play a vital role in helping clients unlock the full value of their data. In this highly collaborative and client-facing role, you will lead data onboarding initiatives for some of our most strategic clients, partnering with internal teams and client stakeholders to ensure data is delivered, validated, and integrated successfully.

As a Data Onboarding Analyst, you will serve as the central coordinator for data onboarding projects, guiding clients through requirements gathering, data acquisition, file specifications, onboarding timelines, and issue resolution. You'll work closely with teams across Data Management, Data Acquisition, Product, and Implementation to ensure projects stay on track, risks are proactively managed, and clients have a smooth and positive experience throughout the process.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys combining project management, relationship management, and data-focused problem solving. You'll gain exposure to healthcare analytics and data operations while developing expertise in managing complex data initiatives, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and delivering meaningful results for clients. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy building strong relationships, and take pride in keeping projects organized and moving forward, we'd love to hear from you.

Roles & Responsibilities

› Lead the successful onboarding and implementation of assigned clients by coordinating cross-functional teams, driving project execution, managing risks, and ensuring a seamless client experience

 Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Business Administration, Engineering, Operations Research, Math, Finance, or related discipline

Job Summary

Research Assistant will work with Dr. Julie Price on imaging studies at the Athinoula A. Martinos Center for Biomedical Imaging, Mass General Brigham Department of Radiology. rows.title: Research Associate, Protein Production
rows.descriptionText:
What if… you could pioneer a new approach to designing life’s most essential molecules?

FL116, backed by Flagship Pioneering, is an early-stage biotechnology company transforming the way biomolecules are synthesized. Our innovative platform has the potential to redefine how critical research, diagnostic, and therapeutic molecules are designed and built. We are seeking passionate problem solvers ready to make a profound impact on biotechnology and therapeutic innovation.

Position Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated and exceptionally organized Research Associate II to expand our protein production capabilities across two complementary scales: bulk expression and purification of individual high-priority targets, and high-throughput parallel production of large variant panels. This hands-on, laboratory-facing role will execute and advance scalable protein expression, purification, normalization, and characterization workflows that feed the design–build–test cycles at the core of our platform.

The successful candidate will bring direct, practical experience in recombinant protein production and chromatographic purification at both preparative and high-throughput scale — together with the ability to execute experiments, run high-throughput analytics, troubleshoot workflows, and deliver well-characterized protein reagents on rapid timelines. This individual will work closely with Protein Engineering, Chemistry, and Assay Development team to align production activities with program priorities and experimental timelines. Meticulous record-keeping and sample traceability are essential to this role. Experience with liquid handlers, magnetic-bead purification platforms such as the KingFisher, cell-free expression, or workflow scripting is preferred.

The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, enjoys solving technical challenges, and is motivated to apply automation and emerging technologies to developing a synthetic biology platform.

Key Responsibilities

Bulk Expression & Purification

Execute multi-liter recombinant expression campaigns in bacteria from construct transformation and culture growth through induction, harvest, and lysis. Design, build, and run preparative purification methods on ÄKTA FPLC systems using UNICORN, including affinity, ion exchange, size exclusion, and mixed-mode chromatography. Deliver milligram-to-gram quantities of highly pure, well-characterized protein. Troubleshoot expression and purification challenges such as low yield, insolubility, aggregation, and proteolysis, and drive protocol improvements that increase yield and purity. 

High-Throughput Production & Analytics

Bacterial library transformation, colony picking and sequencing Execute miniaturized, parallel protein expression and purification in plate-based formats Perform automated purification, sample normalization, and quality assessment to deliver fit-for-purpose protein reagents at scale. Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and continuously improve liquid handlers, magnetic-bead purification platforms (e.g., KingFisher), automated purification systems, and associated analytical instrumentation. Run high-throughput protein analytics across many samples in parallel, including plate-based quantitation, capillary electrophoresis, analytical SEC/SEC-HPLC, and thermal stability or aggregation screening. Translate methods between scales — adapting preparative purifications into miniaturized high-throughput formats, and scaling promising hits back up for in-depth characterization. 

Required Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, bioengineering, synthetic biology or a related scientific discipline with 1-4 years s of relevant academic and/or industry experience; or a master’s degree with 0-2 years of commercial experience. Hands-on experience with recombinant protein expression and production workflows in E. coli, including multi-liter culture growth and harvest. Direct, hands-on experience operating ÄKTA FPLC systems, including independently designing, executing, and troubleshooting purification methods in UNICORN — not solely running pre-established protocols. Demonstrated proficiency across multiple column purification modalities. Demonstrated experience working at both scales: preparative purification of individual targets to milligram-or-greater quantities, and parallel, plate-based production and analytics across large sample sets. Exceptional organization and record-keeping, with a proven ability to track samples, buffers, and method runs in parallel without loss of traceability. Core molecular biology skills, including plasmid preparation, cloning, and transformation. Ability to independently execute experiments, analyze data, troubleshoot technical problems, maintain accurate documentation, and advance assigned work. Ability to maintain flexibility in the face of evolving priorities and short timelines in a collaborative, matrixed research environment. Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with a clear commitment to laboratory safety and data integrity. 

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with magnetic-bead–based purification platforms such as the Thermo KingFisher. Familiarity with cell-free or yeast expression systems. Hands-on experience programming and operating liquid handlers and robotic workstations (e.g., Hamilton, Tecan, Opentrons, Bravo). Comfort organizing and analyzing experimental data in Excel, Python, or similar tools, and maintaining structured records in an ELN or LIMS. 

Who You Are

Innovative Pioneer: You are excited to help build new production capabilities and continually look for better ways to make and characterize protein.

Collaborative Contributor: You work effectively across disciplines, partnering closely with scientists in protein engineering, assay development, automation, machine learning, and beyond.

Inventive Problem Solver: You proactively identify challenges and rapidly develop creative, practical solutions.

Comfortable at Any Scale: You move easily between a careful multi-step purification of a single important target and a plate of ninety-six variants, and you bring the same rigor to both.

Rigorously Organized: You keep meticulous records, design your workflows so results are reproducible months later, and are trusted by colleagues to know exactly where every sample stands.

Mission-Driven Individual: You are motivated by the opportunity to fundamentally transform how biomolecules are designed and synthesized, with meaningful impact on human health and biotechnology.

More About Flagship Pioneering

Flagship Pioneering conceives, creates, resources, and develops first-in-category life sciences companies to transform human health and sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, generating billions in value. Flagship companies are known for addressing humanity’s most pressing challenges and advancing innovative solutions with global impact.

We are an equal opportunity employer and are dedicated to building diverse and inclusive teams. If you have some of the qualifications listed above but not all, we still encourage you to apply. We value passion, experience in many forms, and unique backgrounds.

Come pioneer the future with us.

About The Operations Analyst Program

The Operations Analyst Program is an early-career development opportunity for driven recent and soon-to-be graduates who want to launch a career at the intersection of investment management, operations, data, and technology. Analysts use analytical, technical, and collaborative skills to help deliver operational excellence, solve business challenges, and improve outcomes for clients.

As investment operations evolve through data, automation, and AI, analysts gain hands-on experience supporting business-critical investment processes while helping identify opportunities to improve how work gets done. Through ownership of operational processes and exposure to continuous improvement, data analytics, automation, workflow design, and AI, analysts strengthen controls, improve decision-making, and contribute to scalable solutions that support clients and business growth.

Over three weeks, Analysts begin as a cohort with an immersion in Parametric's investment strategies, operating model, and Operations organization. Following onboarding, analysts join teams supporting Market, Client, or Control functions, where they develop domain expertise, learn business-critical workflows, and build an end-to-end understanding of how Operations supports clients, portfolios, risk management, and business growth.

Operations teams are responsible for the execution, oversight, servicing, and control activities that support the investment lifecycle. Analysts work closely with teammates and stakeholders across the organization to execute processes accurately, resolve operational challenges, improve controls, and deliver exceptional client outcomes.

In addition to their core team responsibilities, analysts may collaborate with specialized teams within Operations focused on process transformation, analytics, workflow modernization, automation, and AI-enabled solutions. Partnering with subject matter experts across Market, Client, and Control functions to identify opportunities, redesign processes, and implement scalable improvements that enhance operational effectiveness. Through this partnership, analysts may gain exposure to transformation initiatives while continuing to build deep operational expertise.

The program is designed for people who are curious about how businesses operate, motivated to improve processes, and eager to continue learning. As business needs evolve, analysts may gain exposure to different Operations functions, participate in cross-functional initiatives, or contribute to transformation efforts, broadening their knowledge, experience, and skill sets.

What You'll Do And Learn

Learn Parametric's investment strategies, operating model, and business-critical Operations workflows, and understand how Market, Client, and Control functions support clients, portfolios, risk management, and business growth.Learn and execute business-critical investment operations workflows accurately and on time. Responsibilities may include activities such as cash and position reconciliation, trade lifecycle support, client servicing, corporate actions, account onboarding and maintenance, contracts, oversight activities, and billing, depending on team assignment.Develop an end-to-end understanding of assigned processes, including activities, decisions, systems, data flows, controls, handoffs, and upstream and downstream dependencies.Investigate exceptions, breaks, recurring operational issues, and client-impacting events using structured problem-solving and data analysis. Identify root causes, assess impacts, and recommend sustainable solutions.Partner with Operations teams, portfolio managers, traders, sales, product management, technology teams, external providers, and other stakeholders to resolve issues, improve handoffs, and support business priorities.Perform quality control and verification activities, maintain accurate records and documentation, and help ensure operational processes meet established policies, procedures, and control standards.Analyze operational and investment data to identify patterns, anomalies, trends, bottlenecks, and emerging risks. Build reports, dashboards, or analytical tools that turn data into actionable insights and improvement opportunities.Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, or redesign workflows and contribute to process mapping, requirements gathering, testing, implementation, and adoption activities.Collaborate with Automation, Reinvention & Collaboration (ARC) and other partners on process-improvement initiatives, workflow modernization efforts, analytics projects, automation solutions, and AI-enabled capabilities.Use or learn tools such as Excel, Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI, SQL, Python, workflow automation platforms, process-modeling tools, and approved AI solutions, as appropriate to the assignment.Contribute to operational excellence, analytics, automation, or process-improvement initiatives and present findings, recommendations, and outcomes to team members and business partners.

What You'll Bring

Associate or bachelor's degree completed by the program start date. Relevant fields may include industrial, process, or systems engineering; operations research; supply chain; data science or analytics; computer science; information systems; mathematics; statistics; finance; accounting; economics; or a related analytical, business, or technical field. Candidates from other majors with relevant quantitative, technical, or process-improvement experience are also encouraged to apply.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to break down ambiguous issues, work with data, identify root causes, and form well-supported conclusions.A systems-thinking and continuous-improvement mindset, including curiosity about how people, processes, data, controls, and technology interact end to end and a desire to make work simpler, more accurate, efficient, scalable, and controlled.High attention to detail and a commitment to quality, sound judgment, risk awareness, responsible use of data and technology, and positive client outcomes.Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with teammates and stakeholders and communicate complex ideas in a clear and organized manner.Ownership, learning agility, adaptability, and the ability to prioritize effectively in a collaborative, deadline-driven environment.Experience using spreadsheets to organize and analyze information and communicate findings, or the ability to learn quickly.Strong interest in building a career at the intersection of investment management, operations, process improvement, data, and technology.Ability to work full-time (40 hours per week) by the program start date.

Preferred Qualifications

Coursework, internships, or project experience involving process mapping, continuous improvement, business analysis, data analysis, automation, workflow design, programming, analytics, or AI.Exposure to one or more tools such as Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI, SQL, Python, workflow automation platforms, process-modeling tools, version control platforms, or similar technologies.Familiarity with financial markets, investment management, or business operations. Prior investment operations experience is not required.Experience contributing to a cross-functional project, presenting recommendations, developing a prototype, or helping others adopt a new process, workflow, or technology solution.

Hybrid (3 days in office, 2 remote)

rows.title: AI Enablement Engineer
rows.descriptionText:
Brooks is a leading provider of automation solutions with over 40 years of experience in the semiconductor industry, offering precision robotics, integrated automation systems, and contamination control solutions that empower chip manufacturers worldwide. Our product portfolio includes a range of automation solutions, including robots, vacuum systems, and atmospheric robots for semiconductor manufacturing (www.brooks.com).

Are you looking for a place where you can be part of a transformation? Join us at Brooks Automation and be a part of a dynamic organization that is shaping the future of technology.

AI Enablement Engineer

Job Description
Brooks Automation is seeking an AI Enablement Engineer to join the Engineering organization. This role offers the opportunity to directly influence how engineering work is done at Brooks Automation. The AI Enablement Engineer will help shape the responsible adoption of AI across engineering teams, improving efficiency while preserving the rigor and quality required for advanced automation products. In this role, you will support the identification, evaluation, development, and deployment of AI tools and workflows that improve engineering productivity across systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, and software engineering disciplines.

This position is engineering‑focused and hands‑on. The AI Enablement Engineer will work closely with engineers and engineering leadership to integrate AI tools and develop custom AI agents that support real engineering work such as design creation, drawing and schematic review, analysis, documentation, requirements understanding, and engineering data access.

Success in this role is measured by practical, measurable improvements in engineering efficiency, while maintaining Brooks standards for quality, data security, and IP protection.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Evaluate and apply AI tools that improve engineering efficiency across mechanical, electrical, and software disciplines.Design, develop, and maintain custom AI agents, and lightweight automation tools that support day‑to‑day engineering activities.Identify recurring engineering problems and translate them into repeatable, AI‑enabled solutions.Integrate AI tools and agents into existing engineering workflows rather than creating parallel processes.Partner with engineering teams to pilot AI solutions and refine them based on real usage and feedback.Develop and document best practices for responsible AI usage within engineering.Work with IT and Security teams to ensure AI tools and agents comply with Brooks data security, IP protection, and governance requirements.Support training and enablement for engineers adopting AI tools and workflows.Define and track before‑and‑after productivity metrics to quantify the impact of AI adoption on engineering outcomes.Provide regular feedback to engineering leadership on AI effectiveness, limitations, and opportunities for expansion.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

Bachelor’s Degree in an Engineering related discipline.In depth knowledge of modern AI tools and their application to technical and engineering tasks.Experience improving engineering tools, processes, or development efficiency.Strong understanding of engineering workflows and deliverables.Strong problem‑solving skills and ability to work across engineering disciplines.Experience developing automation, scripts, internal tools, or AI‑enabled agents to support engineering workflows is a plus.Familiarity with engineering systems such as CAD/ECAD tools, software development environments, FEA/Simulation and PLM systems is a plus.Experience supporting engineering productivity or digital transformation initiatives is a plus.Ability to work effectively in a fast‑moving, evolving technical environment is a plus.

Compensation
Base Salary Range: $105,593.46 USD to $142,861.74 USD

Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus.

rows.title: Bioinformatics Scientist I
rows.descriptionText:
About The Job

The Scientist I, Bioinformatics develops novel methods for detecting, reporting and analyzing alterations in tumor DNA and RNA, while optimizing existing methods. The incumbent provides scientific and technical contributions for a designated project on an interdisciplinary team. The Scientist I, Bioinformatics is also responsible for supporting novel biomarker and companion diagnostics development by mining and analyzing various types of data generated during the product development and validation process.

Key Responsibilities

Partner within an interdisciplinary team of Biochemists, Bioinformatics Scientists, Computational Biologists, Data Scientists, focused on developing diagnostic products using massively parallel sequencing of tumor genomic DNA and RNA.Contribute to the development of new methods and algorithms to identify and characterize alterations in tumor DNA and RNA derived from clinical cancer specimens.Enhance existing methods, improving their assay capabilities as well as their technical robustness.Process, analyze, and interpret high volumes of data for the development and validation of methods.Monitor and evaluate analytical aspects of new and emerging technologies.Present scientific and technical data to colleagues in a clear and cohesive manner.Prepare project timetables, schedules and deliverables.Provide independent contributions.Other duties as assigned.Comply with FMI's attendance policies

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

Master’s Degree in Biochemistry, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Computer Science or similar discipline1+ years of industry or academic medical center professional experience or post-doctorate workProficiency with programming and scripting languages R and Python

Preferred Qualifications

PhD degree in Biochemistry, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Computer Science or similar discipline3+ years of industry experienceStrong scientific understanding of molecular biology and genomicsFacility with additional programming and scripting languagesExperience contributing to a complex production analytical systemExperience developing algorithms for analysis of biological dataPrior experience with high-throughput sequencingExperience in cancer research, including a working understanding of computational approaches for cancer genome analysisExcellent teamwork, time management and organizational skillsAbility to work independently in a multidisciplinary, fast-paced, dynamic, and results-oriented environmentAbility to present data to a multidisciplinary audience in a clear and cohesive mannerUnderstanding of HIPAA and importance of privacy of patient dataStrong interpersonal skills that include collaboration and creative problem solvingImpeccable documentation practices and attention to detailThe ability to prioritize and complete tasks in a timely mannerUnderstanding of HIPAA and the importance of patient data privacyCommitment to reflect FMI’s values: Integrity, Courage, and Passion

A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance. This position also qualifies for Foundation Medicine's benefits.

rows.descriptionText:

We are seeking highly motivated undergraduate/graduate students for a temporary research internship opportunity within our team at Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH).The project is focused on advancing computational methods for medical imaging and exploring emerging hybrid quantum-classical computing approaches for healthcare applications. Interns will have the opportunity to work at the intersection of quantum computing, computational imaging, medical physics, artificial intelligence, and biomedical data science, contributing to research that may help shape the future of PET/CT imaging and related technologies.
Expected ResponsibilitiesAssist in the development and evaluation of computational algorithms for large-scale medical imaging applications.Contribute to research involving hybrid quantum-classical computing frameworks.Implement, optimize, and benchmark algorithms using modern scientific computing tools.Support simulation studies, image analysis, and quantitative performance evaluation.Work with high-performance computing resources, GPU-accelerated computing environments, and emerging quantum computing platforms.Participate in research discussions, software development, manuscript preparation, and presentation of scientific results.
Minimum QualificationsCurrent undergraduate or graduate student in Computer Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Medical Physics, or a related field.Proficiency in Python and MATLAB programming.Familiarity with scientific computing, numerical methods, and data analysis.Strong analytical, mathematical, and problem-solving skills.Ability to work independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary research team.Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Preferred QualificationsExperience with medical imaging, image processing, signal processing, computational physics, or scientific computing.Experience with machine learning, optimization algorithms, or scientific software development.Familiarity with GPU computing, CUDA, parallel computing, or high-performance computing environments.Exposure to quantum computing concepts and/or frameworks such as Qiskit, CUDA-Q, PennyLane, Cirq, or related platforms.Previous research experience and interest in contributing to scientific publications and conference presentations.Interest in translational healthcare technologies and next-generation medical imaging systems.
The position is open to undergraduate students, though graduate students and applicants with prior research experience are especially encouraged to apply.

rows.title: Senior Data Scientist, Predictive Immune Biomarker Foundation Models
rows.descriptionText:
Job Description

Senior Scientist, Predictive Immune Biomarkers (R3)

The Precision Genetics group within the Data, AI and Genome Sciences Department is seeking a Senior Scientist to join our Computational Precision Immunology team in Cambridge, MA. We are looking for a skilled data scientist with extensive experience to develop predictive biomarkers in immunology based on multi-modal and multi-scale data analyses.

Key Responsibilities

Foundation Models: Build, fine-tune, troubleshoot, and benchmark foundation models for predictive immune biomarker discovery.Multi-omics Analysis: Perform quality control (QC) and analysis of different molecular data types including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., Limma, Seurat, scanpy), spatial transcriptomics (e.g., CosMx, 10x Visium), and proteomics (e.g., OLINK, mass spectrometry-based approaches).Multi-omics Integration: Integrate multi-omics datasets, including gene/protein expression, spatial transcriptomics, and genotype data.Documentation: Prepare detailed documentation of analysis methods and results in a timely manner.

Required Qualifications

Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, AI/ML, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genetics & Genomics, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Pharmaceutical Science, or related STEM field.A proven track record in multi-omics analysis.Hands-on experience with building, fine-tuning, benchmarking foundation models, preferably for patient stratification related downstream tasks.Fundamental understanding of AI/ML methods, multi-omics data analysis, and omics integration (e.g., RNA-Seq, single-cell RNA-Seq, genotype, spatial transcriptomics, OLINK).Proficiency in R, Python, and Bash, with the ability to establish best practices for reproducible data analyses.Experience with high-performance computing (HPC) systems and AWS Cloud Services (e.g., IAM, S3 buckets).A collaborative and self-motivated individual with a strong work ethic, capable of managing multiple objectives in a dynamic environment and adapting to changing priorities.Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Good understanding of autoimmune disease biology.Experience in processing and analyzing real-world data.Familiarity with spatial transcriptomics analysis.Knowledge of statistical and population genetics principles.

Required Skills

Autoimmune Diseases, Biomarkers, Cellular Immunology, Computational Biology, Data Science, Genetic Analysis, High Performance Computing (HPC), Immunology Research, Machine Learning (ML), Omics, RNA-Seq, Stratification, Transcriptomics

rows.title: AI Enablement Engineer
rows.descriptionText:
Brooks is a leading provider of automation solutions with over 40 years of experience in the semiconductor industry, offering precision robotics, integrated automation systems, and contamination control solutions that empower chip manufacturers worldwide. Our product portfolio includes a range of automation solutions, including robots, vacuum systems, and atmospheric robots for semiconductor manufacturing (www.brooks.com).

Are you looking for a place where you can be part of a transformation? Join us at Brooks Automation and be a part of a dynamic organization that is shaping the future of technology.

AI Enablement Engineer

Job Description
Brooks Automation is seeking an AI Enablement Engineer to join the Engineering organization. This role offers the opportunity to directly influence how engineering work is done at Brooks Automation. The AI Enablement Engineer will help shape the responsible adoption of AI across engineering teams, improving efficiency while preserving the rigor and quality required for advanced automation products. In this role, you will support the identification, evaluation, development, and deployment of AI tools and workflows that improve engineering productivity across systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, and software engineering disciplines.

This position is engineering‑focused and hands‑on. The AI Enablement Engineer will work closely with engineers and engineering leadership to integrate AI tools and develop custom AI agents that support real engineering work such as design creation, drawing and schematic review, analysis, documentation, requirements understanding, and engineering data access.

Success in this role is measured by practical, measurable improvements in engineering efficiency, while maintaining Brooks standards for quality, data security, and IP protection.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Evaluate and apply AI tools that improve engineering efficiency across mechanical, electrical, and software disciplines.Design, develop, and maintain custom AI agents, and lightweight automation tools that support day‑to‑day engineering activities.Identify recurring engineering problems and translate them into repeatable, AI‑enabled solutions.Integrate AI tools and agents into existing engineering workflows rather than creating parallel processes.Partner with engineering teams to pilot AI solutions and refine them based on real usage and feedback.Develop and document best practices for responsible AI usage within engineering.Work with IT and Security teams to ensure AI tools and agents comply with Brooks data security, IP protection, and governance requirements.Support training and enablement for engineers adopting AI tools and workflows.Define and track before‑and‑after productivity metrics to quantify the impact of AI adoption on engineering outcomes.Provide regular feedback to engineering leadership on AI effectiveness, limitations, and opportunities for expansion.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

Bachelor’s Degree in an Engineering related discipline.In depth knowledge of modern AI tools and their application to technical and engineering tasks.Experience improving engineering tools, processes, or development efficiency.Strong understanding of engineering workflows and deliverables.Strong problem‑solving skills and ability to work across engineering disciplines.Experience developing automation, scripts, internal tools, or AI‑enabled agents to support engineering workflows is a plus.Familiarity with engineering systems such as CAD/ECAD tools, software development environments, FEA/Simulation and PLM systems is a plus.Experience supporting engineering productivity or digital transformation initiatives is a plus.Ability to work effectively in a fast‑moving, evolving technical environment is a plus.

Compensation
Base Salary Range: $105,593.46 USD to $142,861.74 USD

Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus.

rows.title: Technical Associate I
rows.descriptionText:
Posting Description

TECHNICAL ASSOCIATE I, Comp Sci & Artificial Intelligence Lab , works support an active research program at the intersection of immersive teleoperation and learned manipulation policies, with a focus on robot legibility, making learned robot behavior interpretable and predictable to the humans working alongside it. The Technical Associate will build and maintain the lab's VR-based teleoperation and data-collection infrastructure, support the collection and curation of robot demonstration datasets, and assist in training, deploying, and evaluating vision-language-action (VLA) policies on physical multi-arm and dexterous manipulation platforms. This is a hands-on research engineering role with substantial intellectual scope: the person in this position will contribute to experimental design and to publications, not only to system maintenance.

The full job description is available, here: https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/j7o8p3ws4wqo3b2llzqed/Technical-Associate-1-sept..-2026-Bobu.docx?rlkey=mioxm2nt7qju2fh1q269qnf5t&st=j522isjy&dl=0

Job Requirements

REQUIRED : Bachelor's degree in computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience; strong programming ability in Python; demonstrated hands-on experience with physical robot systems including at least one of: manipulator control, teleoperation, motion planning, or robot hardware integration; working knowledge of ROS or ROS 2; practical experience training and evaluating deep learning models in PyTorch; demonstrated ability to debug across the full stack: hardware, drivers, middleware, and learning code; and ability to work independently on open-ended problems, and to communicate technical findings clearly in writing and in discussion.

This position is well suited to someone with a bachelor's or master's degree who intends to pursue graduate study in robotics and wants a period of deep, full-time research experience beforehand.

This is a 1-year funded position, with possibility of extension.

Co-op – Software Engineer (R&D) – Cambridge, MA – January - August 2027

Job Description

Are you interested in an Internship opportunity with Philips? We welcome individuals who are currently pursuing a graduate (MS) degree to participate in paid intern opportunities. Through this role you will gain meaningful, hands-on experience working for a HealthTech company.

Your Role

Developing applications and components within a highly motivated software development team focused on the creation of next generation medical information systems -and applications.Learning and contributing to solving problems with our highly experienced architects and software development team.Working in an environment that embodies and embraces new ideas and innovations through agile methodologies and innovation marathons.Pushing the innovation and technology boundaries to bring breakthrough solutions to complex clinical and business problems.Utilizing software design patterns to enhance software quality by addressing fundamental challenges in large-scale system development. These challenges include communication of architectural knowledge among developers, accommodating new design paradigms or architectural styles, and avoiding development traps and pitfalls that are usually learned only by experience.

You're The Right Fit If

Additionally, familiarity with data analytics, AI tools, data visualization, and business intelligence platforms is advantageous. Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help improve the lives of others.

Philips Transparency Details

Details About Our Benefits Can Be Found Here.

rows.title: Data Analytics & Visualization Analyst - Clearance Required
rows.descriptionText:
About Partner ForcesPartner Forces is a management consulting firm helping homeland security organizations solve some of their most pressing and complex challenges. We partner with government agencies and industry to strengthen national security and critical infrastructure through expertise in strategy, program management, stakeholder engagement, technology implementation, preparedness, and business transformation.
At Partner Forces, we're more than consultants - we're trusted advisors. We work alongside our clients to solve meaningful problems, deliver actionable solutions, and make a lasting impact. As a growing firm, every employee has the opportunity to contribute not only to our clients' success, but also to the future of Partner Forces. We believe great consultants are developed through collaboration, mentorship, continuous learning, and meaningful opportunities to lead.
Our culture is grounded in six core values: Integrity, Excellence, Positivity, Candor, Determination, and Teamwork. These values shape how we work with our clients, support one another, and grow together. We believe that when our people thrive, our clients do too, which is why we invest in our employees' well-being, professional development, and long-term success.
What We Are Looking ForPartner Forces is seeking a Cleared Data Analytics & Visualization Analyst to support a Department of Homeland Security cybersecurity program. We’re looking for someone who combines strong analytical skills with the communication and consulting skills needed to work directly with customers, understand their needs, and turn data into meaningful insights. This role will initially focus on data analysis, reporting, visualization, and development of analytic products, with the opportunity to evolve into broader technical program and PMO support. The right person does not need to be a software developer, but should be technically curious, comfortable working alongside technical teams, and able to understand and translate conversations about data, systems, and technology.
What You'll DoAnalyze program and operational data to identify trends, insights, risks, and opportunities.Develop dashboards, reports, visualizations, and other analytic products that make complex information easier to understand and act on.Engage directly with customers and stakeholders to gather requirements, understand business needs, and translate those needs into useful data and technology solutions.Present findings and recommendations clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.Support recurring and ad hoc reporting and help improve or automate existing reporting processes.Work alongside technical teams to understand requirements, dependencies, risks, and priorities across data and software initiatives.Support technical program management activities, including tracking requirements, decisions, deliverables, action items, and project progress.Participate in technical discussions involving databases, data schemas, software systems, integrations, and related technologies.Support data governance, documentation, process development, and continuous improvement efforts.Adapt to evolving program needs and take on new responsibilities as the program and technical environment mature.
QualificationsUS Citizenship required.Bachelors degree required.Secret clearance required.Experience in data analysis, business analytics, program analysis, or a related field.Strong data visualization and storytelling skills, with experience developing reports, dashboards, or other analytic products.Experience working directly with customers or stakeholders to gather, clarify, and translate requirements.Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and nontechnical audiences.Experience with or exposure to Python or R; advanced programming expertise is not required.Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities.Ability and interest in learning new systems, technologies, and technical concepts.Experience with Power BI, Databricks, ServiceNow, Power Automate, or similar tools preferred but not required.Familiarity with database concepts, data schemas, data governance, or software development environments preferred.ServiceNow administration or development experience is a plus.Previous experience supporting federal government clients or exposure to cybersecurity programs is a plus.Next StepsIf your application looks like a match, someone from our People Operations team will reach out to schedule a phone screening. During this conversation, we will determine if the current or future position aligns with your experience and skills. If things go well, from there you'll meet with members from the project team, including the hiring manager and teammates, and possibly be asked to submit a writing assessment to showcase your practical knowledge. If we find you are a match, you’ll get a call offering you the role. While we wish we could hire every great candidate who comes our way, the reality is that we can't. If you are not selected, we will be sure to connect with you and let you know so you can move on with your search. We will also keep your resume for future needs.

We are committed to fostering a workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. rows.title: Senior Data Analyst - Analytics & Transformation
rows.descriptionText:
At Capital One, data is at the center of everything we do. When we launched as a startup we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Analyst at Capital One you will leverage analytic and technical skills to innovate, build, and maintain well-managed data solutions and capabilities to tackle business problems. The Enterprise Data team is focused on maximizing the value of our data ecosystem and enabling real-time, intelligent experiences built on a scalable, future ready foundation. We are a highly collaborative, cross-functional team working across Product, Technology, Design, Risk, and other partners to build a modern enterprise data ecosystem.

We are looking for an exceptional and innovative Senior Data Analyst to solve complex business and product challenges across our Enterprise Data Product teams. You will lead Product Analytics to measure and improve the performance and health of our Products and Platforms, transforming complex data into actionable, AI-enabled insights that shape product strategy and drive better decisions. If you are a strategic thinker who thrives on solving complex problems and using Data and AI to influence product development, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

On any given day you will be challenged by three types of work – Innovation, Business Intelligence and Data Management:

Innovation

Use Open Source/Digital technologies to mine complex, voluminous, and different varieties of data sources and platforms Build well-managed data solutions, tools, and capabilities to enable self-service frameworks for data consumersDemonstrate ability to explore and quickly grasp new technologies to progress varied initiatives

Business Intelligence

Partner with the business to provide consultancy and translate the business needs to design and develop tools, techniques, metrics, and dashboards for insights and data visualizationDrive analysis that provides meaningful insights on business strategies

Data Management

Drive an understanding and adherence to the principles of data quality management including metadata, lineage, and business definitionsWork collaboratively with appropriate Tech teams to manage security mechanisms and data access governanceBuild and execute tools to monitor and report on data quality

Our ideal candidate will have:

Degree specialized in a Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics disciplineScripting experience in (Python, R, Spark, and SQL)Strong desire and experience with data in various forms (data warehouses/SQL, unstructured data)Experience utilizing and developing within Snowflake services

Basic Qualifications:

Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining a Bachelor’s Degree in quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science or a related quantitative field) plus at least 2 years of experience performing data analytics, or currently has, or is in the process of obtaining a Master’s Degree with an expectation that required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date.  At least 1 year of experience working with at least one scripting language  At least 1 year of experience utilizing business intelligence visualization tool  At least 1 year of experience querying, analyzing and working with data languages and platforms

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s Degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics disciplineAt least 2 years of experience coding in Python, R, Spark, or SQLAt least 2 years of experience working within process management and improvement methodologies – Agile, Lean, Six Sigma, etc. At least 1 year of experience utilizing and developing within AWS servicesAt least 1 year of experience working with and demonstrating knowledge of data governance, data quality management concepts and data quality tools (i.e. Informatica DQ)

rows.title: Business Analyst Intern (Summer 2027)
rows.descriptionText:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Business Analyst team shapes the strategy, growth, and performance of Robinhood's credit products, delivering top-tier experiences for our users. As part of the broader Credit organization, we work closely with product, engineering, risk, and operations to unlock sustainable business growth through deep analytical rigor. Our team fosters a collaborative, ownership-driven culture where every analyst directly influences business strategy and product direction.

As a Business Analyst Intern, you'll spend 12 weeks embedded within a team across our Money and Growth org, getting direct exposure to the metrics, stakeholders, and strategic priorities that drive Robinhood's core business. You'll own real work from day one and build the analytical and cross-functional skills that define our team. Top performers may be extended an offer to join our 18-month rotational Business Analyst program after graduation.

This role is based in our Washington, DC office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. 

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

Get hands-on with a specific business area within Money and Growth, working directly with product, engineering, risk, or operations stakeholders on live prioritiesAnalyze business performance metrics and economic drivers to identify growth opportunities and optimize business outcomesStructure and solve complex, ambiguous problems across product strategy, pricing, user segmentation, and risk-return trade-offsPartner with engineering, product, risk, and finance teams to execute key strategic initiatives and monitor program efficacyDevelop analytical models, dashboards, and presentations to inform decision-making and influence business direction

What you bring

Experience or coursework in business analysis, strategy, management consulting, financial services, or a quantitative analytical roleStrong proficiency in SQL and quantitative modeling techniquesAbility to synthesize complex quantitative findings into clear, actionable recommendations for cross-functional partnersFluency with AI tools, with a genuine interest in staying current as the tools evolveCurrently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Engineering, Data Science, or a related quantitative field, with an expected graduation date of Spring/Summer 2028

What we offer

Market competitive compensation structureQuarterly lifestyle wallet for personal wellness, learning and development, and moreAccess to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or notTime away including company holidays, paid time off, and sick timeLively office environment with catered meals, fully stocked kitchens, and geo-specific commuter benefits

Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected hourly range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process.

Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC)

$33—$33 USD

Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity.

If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application.

rows.title: Information Systems Security Engineer Level 3 (Government)
rows.descriptionText:
AT&T Global Public Sector is a trusted provider of secure, IP enabled, cloud-based, network solutions and professional services to the Federal Government . We are dedicated to recruiting, developing and empowering a diverse, high-performing workforce that is passionate about what they do, committed to our shared values and dedicated to our customers’ mission.

RIS I is the delivery of regional IT services to the end user. We offer support of end user devices including desktop, workplace peripherals, and voice and video devices. We support local and campus area networks, including wireless and cable plant.

AT&T has an opening for Information Systems Security Engineer to support the team by performing or reviewing technical security assessments of computing environments to identify points of vulnerability, non-compliance with established Information Assurance (AI) standards and regulations, and recommend mitigation strategies.

This is a full-time onsite role based in the location(s) posted and is performed from the designated work location five days per week. No relocation is offered.

Description Of Job Duties/Responsibilities

Provide expert guidance and work product evaluation to one or more security engineers that support engineering teams for the design, development, implementation, evaluation, and integration of secure networking, computing, and enclave environments.Advocate and recommend system-level solutions for the secure development and maintenance of systems.Monitor and suggest improvement to IA policy; Interact with customers, IT staff, and high-level corporate officers to define and achieve required IA objectives.Ensure that the architecture and design of information systems are functional and secure, including program-of-record systems, new and proposed systems, and special purpose environments with platform IT interconnectivity.Prevention and early detection and resolution of risks to high value assets.Architect, design, implement, support, and evaluate security-focused tools and services.Providing software vulnerability remediation advice to software developers and software development teams.Implementing security vulnerability testing tools to provide continuous monitoring and patch verification.Test and evaluate products in a lab environment.Review certification and accreditation (C&A) documentation, providing feedback on completeness and compliance of its content.Knowledge of 800-53 controls, testing information systems for compliance of the controls, and the creation of test cases.Knowledge of incident response and the creation, execution, and reporting of such activities.Knowledge of Firewalls, IDS/IPS, intrusion detection, VLANS, routing and other network security technologies.Knowledge of virtualization technologies including virtual firewalls, networking and segmentation.Knowledge of SIEM technologies such as Splunk and creation of security event related dashboards.Knowledge of Malware identification, containment, and eradication.Knowledge of access control systems, PKI, multi-factor authentication, and entitlements management.Proficient in Microsoft Windows and Linux operating systems.Provide input into the development of security policies and procedures.Evaluate and recommend new and emerging security products and technologies.Participate in projects that develop new intellectual property.Evangelize security within the organization and be an advocate for customer trust.Excellent written and verbal communication skills.Excellent leadership skills and teamwork skills.

Required Clearance: TS/SCI with polygraph. (#ts/sci) (#polygraph)

Required Qualifications

Twenty (20) years of experience as an ISSE on programs and contracts of similar scope, type, and complexity are required. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Assurance, Information Security System Engineering, or related discipline from an accredited college or university is required. A Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Assurance, Information Security System Engineering, or related discipline may be substituted for two (2) years of experience, reducing the requirement to eighteen (18) years of experience. Four (4) years of additional ISSE experience may be substituted for a Bachelor’s degree.

DoD 8570 compliance with IASAE Level 2 is required.

Ready to join our team? Apply today!

Our Information Systems Security Engineer Level 3 (Government)

earns $118,700 - $243,300

 Must be enrolled at an accredited college or university pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, Data Analytics, Engineering, or a related field. rows.title: AI Execution Analyst and Reporting Lead 1 1 1
rows.descriptionText:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

Today's world is fueled by vast amounts of information. Data is more valuable than ever before. Protecting data and information systems is central to doing business, and everyone in EY Information Security has a critical role to play. Join a global team of over 1000 people who collaborate to support the business of EY by protecting EY and client information assets. Our Information Security professionals enable EY to work securely and deliver secure products and services, as well as detect and quickly respond to security events as they happen. Together, the efforts of our dedicated team help protect the EY brand and build client trust.

Within Information Security we blend risk strategy, digital identity, cyber defense, application security and technology solutions as we consider the entire security lifecycle. You will join a team of hardworking, security-focused individuals dedicated to supporting, protecting and enabling the business through innovative, secure solutions that provide speed to market and business value.

The opportunity

As an Associate Director in Information Security, this position leads the application of AI engineering within a global technology program, working closely with program leadership, workstream leads and technologists from across the globe. The position is responsible for the AI agents and automation that produce the program's reporting to senior leadership and to regional teams, and for the technical standards that govern how the program builds with AI.

This position also serves as the AI leader for Technology Assurance, Risk and Policy, guiding teams across the function on where and how to apply AI and agentic AI within our services and processes. This includes identifying which assurance, risk and policy activities are suited to AI, advising teams on the approach to take, and establishing the practices that allow AI to be adopted consistently and safely across the function.

This is a hands-on engineering position at a senior technical grade, with authority across the program and no direct reports. The position runs and builds AI agents and automation using Claude alongside Python, Power Automate, and the Microsoft platform, and determines what work is given to an agent, how agent output is verified, and what remains with people.

Areas of focus

AI Engineering: Building agentic workflows in Claude that complete an entire piece of work, from reading source data through to producing the finished output.Functional AI Leadership: Acting as the AI leader for Technology Assurance, Risk and Policy, guiding teams on where and how to apply AI and agentic AI within the function's services and processes.Automation Delivery: Owning a program's automation estate, including what is automated, how it is built, and how it is supported over time.Assurance of AI Output: Accountability for reporting that is accurate, reconciled and defensible, with verification of agent output built into the systems that produce it.AI Standards and Capability: Setting the technical direction and standards for how the program builds with AI, and developing engineering capability across the program.

Key Responsibilities

Key responsibilities include:

Design, build and operate the AI agents and automation that produce the program's recurring reporting, using Claude and Claude Code, integrated with the enterprise systems.Own the AI and automation roadmap for the program, prioritizing work according to the effort it saves and the risk it reduces.Guide teams across Technology Assurance, Risk and Policy on where and how to apply AI and agentic AI within the function's services and processes, including which activities are suited to AI and the approach to take.Establish the practices that allow AI to be adopted consistently and safely across the function, and support teams in applying them.Establish how AI output is verified, including reconciliation and checks against source data on every run, and define the conditions under which an agent must stop and escalate rather than continue.Set the standards the program builds to for AI use, covering how work is scoped to an agent, prompt and context engineering, testing for repeatability, documentation and the handling of sensitive data.Advise program leadership on where AI is appropriate, including where a conventional solution is the better answer, and on the cost, risk and effort involved.Evaluate developments in AI tooling and models and introduce what is of value to the program.Build automation that is resilient and supportable, with error handling, secure credential management, logging and alerting, held in version control and documented so that it can be maintained by others.Work with IT and Information Security to secure approval, connectivity and ongoing support for AI tooling, and build within firm policy on AI use, data classification and client confidentiality.Represent the program's AI and automation position to senior stakeholders and governance forums.Develop AI engineering capability across the program through reusable components, documented patterns and practical working sessions.

Skills And Attributes For Success

To qualify for the role, you must have

At least 10 years of experience in software, automation or data engineering, including significant time as a senior individual contributor with technical ownership of systems in production.Demonstrable experience building production solutions with Claude, including Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK.Experience designing agentic workflows that complete an end-to-end task.Practical prompt and context engineering, including testing that model output is reliable and repeatable.Strong Python, including automation of document and data workflows with libraries such as python-pptx, python-docx, openpyxl and pandas, or the equivalent.Microsoft platform experience: Power Apps, Power BI, Dataverse, Copilot Studio and Microsoft Graph.Production experience with a major enterprise workflow automation platform such as Power Automate, including error handling and unattended runs.A track record of automating a recurring operational or reporting process end to end, with demonstrable outcomes.Experience building unattended systems that run reliably, including error handling, credential management, logging, alerting and scheduling.Experience working with large datasets drawn from multiple systems, including reconciling them and assessing whether the data supports the conclusions being drawn from it.Experience setting technical standards that other people build to, through review, shared components or documented patterns.A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems or a related discipline, or equivalent work experience.Strong English language communication skills and the ability to work with diverse, globally distributed teams.

Ideally, you'll also have

Experience integrating AI tooling with enterprise systems and data sources.Experience introducing AI tooling into a governed enterprise environment, including the approval and assurance path.Experience evaluating models or agent frameworks and making an adoption recommendation.Experience delivering security, technology risk or audit reporting to a senior audience.Familiarity with vulnerability management data and tooling.Experience coaching or building technical capability in colleagues who are not engineers.Relevant certification in cloud, data or security engineering.

rows.title: Market Research Analyst (Advance Statistics)
rows.descriptionText:
Job Description

About Innovation GMU:

The Innovation Service Line guides clients throughout the innovation journey as they develop and launch new or improved products and services spanning a range of verticals. This is accomplished using best-in-class services, including idea screening, concept testing, product testing, price and line optimization, package testing and volumetric forecasting. The Global Modeling Unit (GMU) team within the Innovation service line are methodological “experts” that provide a variety of value-added services. In most cases, value-added services are advanced multivariate data analyses such as regression, GLM, discriminant analysis, MDS, clustering algorithms, and proprietary procedures.

What makes this role important at Ipsos?

We are seeking a Market Research Analyst with a strong quantitative background and expertise in statistical modeling and experimental research methods. The Research Analyst, Marketing Science is a resource for internal and external clients in the design and analysis of data based on statistical procedures. As a Research Analyst, you will provide expertise in the appropriate use of value-added analytical models, including approaches proprietary to Ipsos.

What You Can Expect To Be Doing

Clean, structure, code, and summarize survey and secondary dataUse statistical software (SPSS, R, etc.) and business software (Excel) to uncover and evaluate solutions, and assist project staff in running statistical analysesApply programming skills (Excel VBA, Python, etc.) to help automate standard statistical procedures and chart creation.Demonstrate your understanding of multivariate analysis and Ipsos proprietary products, and work with Client Service from understanding business questions to design, analysis, and applicationWork from an analytic plan, assemble Excel outputs or PowerPoint decks to provide results and explanations for Client ServiceConsistently ensure the timely delivery of error free work

This might be the job for you if you have:

BS or MS in Statistics, Applied Statistics, Biostatistics, Econometrics, Quantitative Psychology, or a closely related quantitative field.Strong academic foundation in:Experimental design (DOE)Hypothesis testingRegression analysisAnalysis of variance (ANOVA)Linear and generalized linear modelsSampling methodologiesMultivariate statistical analysisExperience designing and analyzing market research studies, including surveys, pricing research, concept testing, and customer insights projects.Ability to design experiments and quasi-experiments to measure causal impact.Experience applying statistical methods to business decision-making.Proficiency with statistical software such as R, SAS, Python, SPSS, or Stata.Experience communicating complex statistical findings to non-technical business stakeholders.
About Us

Ipsos is one of the world’s largest research companies and currently the only one primarily managed by researchers, ranking as a #1 full-service research organization for four consecutive years. With over 75 different data-driven solutions, and presence in 90 markets, Ipsos brings together research, implementation, methodological, and subject-matter experts from around the world, combining thematic and technical experts to deliver top-quality research and insights. Simply speaking, we help the biggest companies solve some of their biggest problems, serving more than 5000 clients across the globe by providing research, data, and insights on their target markets. And we are proud of our continuous efforts in making Ipsos the best place to work!

About The Team

The Innovation Service Line guides clients throughout the innovation journey as they develop and launch new or improved products and services spanning a range of verticals. We help our clients develop the initial idea for a product/service, ensure the fully-articulated description of the product/service resonates with consumers, confirm that prototypes of the product/service properly deliver on consumer expectations, and finetune the full mix prior to launch. This is accomplished using best-in-class services, including idea screening, concept testing, product testing, price and line optimization, package testing and volumetric forecasting.
